title: Metallica frontman James Hetfield blasts entertainers pushing political agendas at concerts
summary: Metallica frontman James Hetfield took aim at concert politics amid Macklemore's removal from Ed Sheeran's tour over "Free Palestine" calls.
story: Tour fallout and planned protests hit Ed Sheeran after rapper Macklemore was dropped from his upcoming concert lineup following anti-Israel comments. Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy defends the decision, stating fans did not pay to hear political rants. Senior correspondent Eric Shawn joins Harris Faulkner to discuss the controversy ahead of the September 19th show.
Metallica frontman James Hetfield is calling out performers who bring political agendas to the stage.

During Metallica's show at the Las Vegas Sphere on Saturday night, the 63-year-old musician took a moment to express his gratitude to fans who traveled to see the heavy metal band and blasted entertainers who turn concerts into political platforms.

"Unless you live in Vegas, you've come a long way to spend some time with Metallica," he said in a video shared on YouTube. "We're grateful for that — your travels, the money you spend, the time it took, thanks for coming to celebrate with us."
GOO GOO DOLLS' JOHN RZEZNIK DRAWS LINE ON POLITICS AT CONCERTS: 'I'M NOT GOING TO LECTURE YOU'
"I just gotta say, Metallica is not here, like some other entertainers, to influence you with their bulls---, OK?," Hetfield continued as the audience clapped and cheered.
Metallica frontman James Hetfield slammed entertainers who use their concerts for political messaging. (Getty Images)
"We are here … no bulls--- … we're here to forget about all the outside s---, OK?" he added. "Metallica's agenda is love, energy and heavy music, baby!"
ED SHEERAN CONCERTGOERS WARN ARTISTS ABOUT SHARING POLITICAL VIEWS: 'YOU'RE GOING TO ALIENATE' FANS
Although Hetfield did not name any artists, several musicians have recently made political statements during their concerts.

Last month, Macklemore was dropped from his remaining scheduled performances on Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour" after the rapper repeatedly called for a "Free Palestine" and performed his pro-Palestinian protest song "Hind's Hall" while opening for the "Shape of You" singer at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.
Hetfield said Metallica would not influence fans with "their bulls---." (Redferns)
MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS

At the time, Macklemore said Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, told Sheeran that the "Thrift Shop" hitmaker "would not be allowed" to perform at the stadium.
Kraft later confirmed that he opposed Macklemore performing at Gillette Stadium, citing the rapper's "recent actions" and what he called a "broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery."
ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT
Following Macklemore's removal, all of Sheeran's remaining opening acts and supporting musicians, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga, pulled out in solidarity with the rapper.
In an Instagram statement, Sheeran said he was not responsible for Macklemore's removal, explaining that the promoter and venues made the decision.
READ IT: ED SHEERAN'S PRE-CONCERT SPEECH TO PHILLY CROWD ABOUT THE GAZA CONTROVERSY

During his show in Philadelphia, Sheeran said he was "appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine" and called the situation in Gaza "catastrophic and unjustifiable," while describing the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks on Israel as "horrific."
Macklemore (left) was dropped from Ed Sheeran's (right) stadium tour over his "Free Palestine" remarks. (Getty Images)

Sheeran has also defended his decision to keep his concerts apolitical. The four-time Grammy winner said his audience includes children and fans from a wide range of backgrounds who "do not expect a political forum" when they attend his shows.
MACKLEMORE SLAMMED AS 'PERFORMATIVE' AFTER ANNOUNCING 'FREE PALESTINE TOUR'

Macklemore subsequently pledged to donate the $1 million he earned opening for Sheeran to organizations providing humanitarian aid to Palestinians. He also announced a three-date "Free Palestine Tour" scheduled for late October.
During the controversy, country singer Zach Bryan wore a "Free Palestine" T-shirt during his sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium in October.
SPRINGSTEEN, OTHER STARS SHARE STAGE WITH HARDCORE LEFTIST GROUPS AT MUSIC FEST
Other musicians who have made political statements during concerts include Bruce Springsteen, Rage Against the Machine's Tom Morello, Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong and Kacey Musgraves.
Zach Bryan wore a "Free Palestine" T-shirt during his sold-out concerts at Gillette Stadium. (Gus Stewart/Redferns)
Meanwhile, Hetfield has long expressed his opposition to mixing music and politics. In a 2016 interview with the BBC, he explained that Metallica steered clear of divisive topics.
MICK JAGGER DOESN'T WANT TO 'LECTURE' FANS, SAYS HIS JOB IS TO MAKE PEOPLE 'HAVE THE BEST TIME'

"There's a lot of polarization going on in the States, and I see it in other places as well," he said. "But it just seems like you have to get more extreme to balance out the other extreme. We've got to find some balance in the middle here somewhere."

"We stay away from politics [and] from religion," Hetfield added. "That just seems to polarize people even more. We all have our own beliefs, but at the end of the day, we're trying to connect with people, and it seems like political views don't do that as much as music does."

In a 2017 interview with the Chilean newspaper La Tercera, Hetfield declined to share his opinion of Donald Trump, who was president at the time, and reiterated his opposition to mixing music and politics.

"Everyone has an opinion about Donald Trump, I think. My opinion stays with me," he said.
"I'm a singer and guitar player in a rock band," Hetfield continued.

"I hate politics," he added. "I don't want to talk about politics. That separates people, and I want to connect them with music. I prefer to stay out of all that, because it polarizes people, because if I say 'I love Trump' or 'I hate Trump,' someone can say 'then I don't like his music anymore,' which is very silly."
Hetfield has long said that he is against mixing music and politics. (Getty Images for Tribeca Festival)

In a 2016 interview with Vulture, Hetfield's Metallica bandmate Lars Ulrich, who has expressed liberal political views and opposition to Trump, said that he and Hetfield had never discussed politics during their decades of performing together.

"I swear to you, I talk to James Hetfield about most things on this planet, but I don't think I've ever willfully had a political conversation with him," he said.

"We've spent 35 years together, and obviously we've been in the same room when the conversation went towards politics, but James and I sitting down in a room and discussing our particular views on something like affordable health care? Never happened," he added.

title: Kelly Clarkson's store callout shows the 'power' of celebrity statements: expert
summary: Kelly Clarkson's viral feud with Brooklyn store Art of Play over a singing bird automaton has PR experts weighing the risks and opportunities.
story: Fox News host Will Cain discusses singer Kelly Clarkson's social media post about her feud with a toy store in Brooklyn, N.Y on 'The Will Cain Show.'
Kelly Clarkson's recent headline-making feud has public relations experts saying the viral attention brings risks for the store, but could create an opportunity if it handles the backlash well.

Over the weekend, Clarkson called out Art of Play, a Brooklyn store known for its collection of toys, games, books, puzzles and other unique items, for allegedly denying her the ability to buy "Molly," a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton.

"Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me," Clarkson wrote.
PR experts have weighed in on Kelly Clarkson's online feud with a small store in Brooklyn, Art of Play. (Matthew Stockman/Getty Images)
"Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale," she continued.
KELLY CLARKSON SLAMS BROOKLYN STORE OVER ‘PRETTY WOMAN’ TREATMENT

Clarkson then compared the encounter to a memorable scene from the 1990 movie "Pretty Woman," in which Julia Roberts’ character, Vivian Ward, is dismissed by a boutique saleswoman who assumes she cannot afford the store’s clothing.
"But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts’ character in ‘Pretty Woman.’ For sure, check it out," Clarkson added.
The singer’s description of the incident echoed the famous "Pretty Woman" scene, in which Vivian returns to the boutique after being rejected and tells the saleswoman, "Big mistake. Big. Huge."
A source told People: "She’s usually very private and public drama like this isn’t her."
"She’s clearly so ticked off that she couldn’t keep quiet about it. Everyone is surprised by how much this whole thing has escalated," the insider told the outlet.
Kelly Clarkson described a recent shopping experience to that of Julia Roberts' character in "Pretty Woman." (Getty Images)

Doug Eldridge, founder of Achilles PR, told Fox News Digital that this debacle speaks to three key points: "1. The power and presumptive veracity of celebrity statements and/or accusations; 2. The staggering pace and scale of social media as a tool of dissemination; 3. The critical need for a crisis communications plan, regardless of the size of your business."
Art of Play posted a response to Clarkson's original social media callout, claiming that they have had "8 million people" bombarding them with hateful messages after the singer's accusations.

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity. Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger,’" the store posted to their Instagram page on Sunday afternoon.
Kelly Clarkson clapped back after the small Brooklyn store responded to her original call out. (Getty Images)
Eldridge continued, "Irrespective of which side you believe, this has proven Winston Churchill’s famous quip: 'A lie gets halfway around the world before the truth gets its pants on in the morning.'"
After the store's Instagram post, Clarkson took to her X account and Instagram stories on Sunday afternoon to respond to their claims.
"Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn't for sale. That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with," Clarkson wrote, adding a thumbs up emoji.

The singer continued: "So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn't happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone "yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can." That all never happened and now it’s not for sale. Okay, cool. So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it," adding a checkmark emoji.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Clarkson added: "And by the way, I obviously support small businesses because I was literally at a small business trying to purchase things. I love small businesses and know they are important and I always support them, but you don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business. It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool. Unfortunately, you aren’t."

Jay Aldebert, chief growth officer at International Services Inc. and creator of the Profit by Design Methodology, told Fox News Digital that there are two ways Art of Play could view Clarkson bringing millions of people's attention to their small business.
WATCH: Kelly Clarkson’s social media callout could have 'devastating effect,' expert says

"I think it can have two effects, right? The first effect is that you've seen people take up the banner in her name, and you see people posting bad reviews or, obviously, there's a lot of comments. So, there is a negativity that can have an effect. She's got a lot of social power. She has 40 million followers and her taking to social media and making a comment, I think you can have a devastating effect," he began.

"But, if I were to make a counter, the counter is that all good press or all good heat or negative or positive heat, I guess is good and what the store does it with it right now I think can be quite eventful for them," Aldebert continued.
Kelly Clarkson attended the 66th Grammy Awards at Crypto.com Arena on Feb. 4, 2024. (Getty Images for The Recording A)

Aldebert, who manages 1,000 people at his own firm, believes Clarkson should have taken her concerns about her treatment at the store to Art of Play's owner before blasting the whole business on social media.

"If I'm Monday morning quarterback on this particular one, I'm going to say the first step you take is reach out to the owner, see if it can be resolved. If, obviously, it's treated as something where they just blow it off or they're rude, too, then I can kind of see, at least you wait out. You have a great weapon, which is your social media presence. And then take that step if necessary. But I would have liked to see that step taken in terms of the contact of the owner," he said.
WATCH: Expert says Kelly Clarkson should have contacted store owner before posting
Aldebert believes the small store in Brooklyn could spin this press nightmare into a positive, lucrative move for their business.

"It could be as simple and again, I'm just you know kind of taking a couple guesses in terms of what I would do in this, but photos with the bird. Why not charge five dollars to do so? You know, make a bunch of T-shirts as it relates to the products that resemble it," he began.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"Let's put those up front. If it's this bird out there then now people are going to want to see because, 'Hey, they wouldn't sell it to Kelly Clarkson. Will they sell it me?' I would increase the price. There's a lot of different aspects that they could be using this to generate more revenue," Aldebert said. "And I hope that they take action and maybe they get more of those birds. They're kind of gonna be like a prized possession for a short period of time."
On Sunday, Art of Play took to social media to "clarify one additional detail" about Clarkson's visit.

"During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly. We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000. We explained all of this to Kelly Clarkson."
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"We also offered to show her a different singing bird automaton, made by a traditional clockmaking shop in Germany, that she could have taken home with her that day. It costs about $2,000. She did not stick around long enough to see it."

Kelly Clarkson doubled down on her original claims, saying that Art of Play refused to sell her the rare bird because it was out of her price range. (Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame)
"We’ve reached out to Kelly directly to try and clear the air," the shop concluded. "We really do wish her the best and hope that someday we can all laugh about this misunderstanding."
A representative for Clarkson did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for additional comment.

title: RJ Mitte, ‘Breaking Bad’ actor who played Walter White Jr., dies at 34
summary: Actor and disability advocate RJ Mitte, who played Walter "Flynn" White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," has died at age 34.
story: Actor RJ Mitte, best known for portraying Walter White Jr. on the hit AMC series, has died at age 34, his representative confirmed to Fox News Digital. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)
RJ Mitte, the actor who played Walter White Jr. on "Breaking Bad," has died.
"It is with profound sadness we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," Mitte's representative told Fox News Digital.

"RJ Mitte was best known for his role as Walter 'Flynn' White Jr. on AMC’s critically acclaimed, award-winning series Breaking Bad. Drawing from his own experience living with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement continued. "Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s."
"Breaking Bad" star RJ Mitte has died at the age of 34. (Unique Nicole/Getty Images)

The statement noted that Mitte also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, which supports philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities.
'BREAKING BAD' ACTOR MARK MARGOLIS DEAD AT 83
Mitte’s cause of death was not immediately disclosed. Like his character on the Emmy Award-winning show, Mitte had cerebral palsy and was a disability rights advocate.
Last week, Mitte appeared on "The Joe Vulpis Podcast" and spoke about how "Breaking Bad" changed his life and on his close relationship with the cast years after the show's finale, TMZ reported.
Mitte starred in all five seasons of the hit series. ((Photo by Paul Archuleta/FilmMagic))

After appearing in TV shows including "Hannah Montana" and "Vegas," Mitte made his career breakthrough at age 15 in 2008 when he landed the role of Walter White Jr., the son of the series' main character and antihero Walter White (Bryan Cranston) and his wife Skyler (Anna Gunn), on "Breaking Bad."
Mitte starred in all five seasons of the hit AMC series, which received 16 Primetime Emmy Awards, two Golden Globe Awards and three Screen Actors Guild Awards during its run from 2008 to 2014.

In 2014, he won a Screen Actors Guild Award alongside the "Breaking Bad" cast for outstanding ensemble performance in a drama series. Mitte was also honored with the SAG-AFTRA Harold Russell Award at the 2013 Media Access Awards, which recognize inclusive portrayals and employment of people with disabilities in media.
The actor played Walter White Jr., the son of Walter White (Bryan Cranston) and his wife Skyler White (Anna Gunn). (Mark Davis/Getty Images)

The actor, who was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at age 3, previously spoke out about using the visibility he gained from "Breaking Bad" to advocate for broader representation of performers with disabilities.
During a 2015 interview with the Badger Herald, he shared that he viewed his disability as a source of strength, saying it helped shape the actor and advocate he became.

"I think everyone that has a disability has the opportunity to make an impact with what they can do and who they are. I wouldn’t be able to do what I do today if it wasn’t for my disability and what it instilled in me," Mitte said.

Mitte often credited "Breaking Bad" with transforming his life and career. He previously said he believed Walter Jr. resonated with the disability community because his cerebral palsy was part of the character, but not the center of his story.
BRYAN CRANSTON DOESN'T MISS 'BREAKING BAD' CHARACTER WALTER WHITE

"Walt Jr. had cerebral palsy but he wasn’t disabled," he said on "ListenABLE" podcast in Sept. 2021. "That’s the biggest thing that I feel is so important when we see characters on television that represent individuals with disabilities. Their disability isn’t what makes them a character. It’s who they are, where they came from and how they got there through determination and strength and that’s what makes them so strong and independent."

Mitt was also a disability rights advocate, ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s, and president of The Mitte Foundation. ((Photo by Noam Galai/Getty Images for Runway Of Dreams Foundation))

After "Breaking Bad" ended, Mitte went on to appear in a recurring role on the hit ABC series "Switched at Birth." His other television work included roles in "Chance," "This Close," "Now Apocalypse" and "The Guardians of Justice (Will Save You!)."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Mitte also appeared in movies including "Who's Driving Doug," "Time Share," "Standing Up for Sunny," "The Oak Room," "Love Me Dead" and "Westhampton." The actor executive produced and starred in the 2021 coming of age film "Triumph," in which he played a high school senior with cerebral palsy who is determined to join his school’s wrestling team.

He most recently starred in the drama "Talking to Strangers," which was released in July. Mitte, who has several upcoming projects listed on IMDB, made his last public appearance at a screening of "Talking to Strangers" in Beverly Hills on Sept. 30, less than two weeks before his death.

In addition to serving as the president of the Mitte Foundation, Mitte was also an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s and worked with SAG-AFTRA’s disability inclusion efforts.
Mitte announced his engagement to his longtime girlfriend Kennedy Suarez in October 2025.
During a podcast appearance last week, Mitte reflected on how he wanted to "top ‘Breaking Bad.’" (Paul Archuleta/Getty Images)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

A few days before his death, Mitte shared his final Instagram post, which included a clip from his appearance on "The Joe Vulpis Podcast" in which he discussed the possibility of continuing the story of Walter White's family following the fictional drug lord's death in the show's finale.
"The White Family Isn’t Over @thejoe #breakingbad," he wrote in the caption.

"I don’t think it was an end; I think it was really the end of Heisenberg’s journey," he said in the clip. "But I don’t think that was the end of Skyler and Walt and Holly’s journey. You know I think there’s a lot of unanswered questions there, that for them will probably never be answered."
"I think there’s still a big step for the White family," Mitte added.
Mitte also admitted that "Breaking Bad," which is widely considered one of the greatest TV shows of all time, set an almost impossible standard for the rest of his career.

"I just want to top ‘Breaking Bad,’ that’s the hardest," he said. "That is literally said, a bar for myself as a young man that is kinda unattainable. I tell people, ‘Look, it’s a long way down from the top of the mountain."

title: Selma Blair arrested after in-flight incident
summary: Selma Blair, 54, was arraigned on two assault charges after she was arrested and hospitalized Sunday in New York. The actress allegedly attacked crew members mid-air on a Delta flight from Los Angeles.
story: The actress was arrested Sunday after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City. (Credit: Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)

Selma Blair was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault for reportedly assaulting a nurse and a police officer after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City, the Associated Press reported.
The judge set bail at $20,000 cash/$60,000 bond/ $60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027.
The actress was arrested Sunday aboard the flight from LA to NYC.

"On Sunday October 11 at approximately 11pm at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938 which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital.
"Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation."
SELMA BLAIR SAYS ‘NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS’ AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT
Selma Blair seen exiting the courthouse in Queens on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)

Blair appeared in Queens Criminal Court in Queens, New York. The actress was arrested Sunday after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
During her court appearance in Queens, Blair’s lawyer claimed the actress missed multiple doses of a "powerful" medication, The New York Post reported.

"This was not an intentional assault," the outlet noted that her attorney, Shawn Barnes, said in court. "Ms. Blair missed several doses of… a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms."

"Ms. Blair boarded this flight after being on set and working extensive hours and exhaustive hours in the days leading up to this flight," he added. "Additionally, at one point, during the flight, there was an incident where Miss Blair actually fell and hit her head," Barnes added, according to The NY Post. "These factors, coupled with altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation."

title: Ben Affleck has blunt response to teenage son's Lamborghini request after infamous mishap
summary: Ben Affleck revealed his son Samuel asked him to buy a Lamborghini, four years after the teen's infamous fender-bender at a luxury car dealership.
story: Actor Ben Affleck defended AI usage in Hollywood during a conversation with Bloombergs Lucas Shaw on Thursday.
Ben Affleck's son Samuel appears to have developed a taste for Lamborghinis, four years after he accidentally backed one into another luxury car.
During a recent appearance on his "Animals" co-star Kerry Washington's podcast, "Street You Grew Up On," the 54-year-old actor said that Samuel, 14, inherited his affinity for luxury items.
Affleck, who shares three children including Samuel, Violet, 20, and Fin, 17, with his ex-wife Jennifer Garner, told Washington that he recently shut down his son's request to buy him a Lamborghini.
BEN AFFLECK ADMITS HIS TEENAGER ROASTED HIS DATING HISTORY WHILE AT DINNER

"I see my son now, you know, and he's a lot like me," Affleck said. "And it makes me realize — because my older two ones — they kind of spoiled me because they're like, 'No, we don't want this. We don't want that.' They're like, aversive."
Ben Affleck shut down his 14-year-old son Samuel's request for him to buy a yellow Lamborghini. (Getty Images)

"My son's like, ‘Dad, you should get a Lambo,’" the Oscar winner recalled with a laugh. "'What? A Lambo? Are you f---ing crazy? Am I an a--hole in a yellow Lamborghini driving around like at the club?' He's like, 'Yeah.'"
ROB LOWE SAYS SON WAS MUGGED AT KNIFEPOINT AFTER IGNORING DAD'S NYC WARNING
"No. No!" Affleck exclaimed as Washington laughed.

Samuel was previously involved in a mishap with a yellow Lamborghini while visiting 777 Exotics, a luxury car rental dealership in the Los Angeles area, with his father and Affleck's then-fiancée, Jennifer Lopez, in June 2022.
At the time, Affleck allowed Samuel, then 10, to sit in the driver's seat of a bright yellow Lamborghini SUV before the boy accidentally put the car into reverse and backed into a white BMW.
Samuel accidentally backed a yellow Lamborghini into a BMW at a luxury car dealership when he was 10. (Getty Images)

Samuel was photographed jumping out of the Lamborghini to inspect the vehicles, while Affleck also checked for damage. The "Gone Girl" star was later photographed hugging Samuel while talking with Lopez, whom he married in July 2022. The former couple finalized their divorce in January 2025.
The vehicle involved in Samuel's incident was a Lamborghini Urus, which rented for $1,475 per day and was valued at $250,000 at the time, according to the New York Post.

At the time, representatives for Affleck and 777 Exotics both told the New York Post there was no damage to either vehicle. An employee at the rental dealership also said there were no hard feelings following the fender-bender.
KRISTIN CAVALLARI ADMITS HER KIDS FLY COACH WHILE SHE SITS IN FIRST CLASS
"Affleck loves cars," the dealership employee told the New York Post. "We hope they come in again."
Affleck previously refused to buy Samuel a $6,000 pair of sneakers. (Getty Images)
The Lamborghini isn't the first high-priced item to catch Samuel's eye.
In March 2025, an exchange between Affleck and Samuel made headlines after Samuel was filmed admiring a $6,000 pair of Dior x Nike Air Jordan 1 sneakers in a video shared on Instagram.
MARK WAHLBERG ADMITS HOLLYWOOD FAME COMES WITH ‘BAGGAGE’ FOR HIS KIDS

In the clip, Affleck and Samuel browsed sneakers at a convention, where Samuel spotted the Dior shoes. After seeing the $6,000 price tag, Affleck told his son, "That's a lot of lawns you gotta mow there."
During an interview with Access Hollywood later that month, Affleck joked about the viral video.
MICHAEL DOUGLAS SAYS KIRK DOUGLAS GAVE HIM $10,000 AT 21 AND TOLD HIM HE WAS ON HIS OWN
"That's what happens when you tell a motherf---er they have to mow a lawn," he told the outlet. "All of a sudden they don't want those shoes, and he was like, ‘But I always said they were tough.’"
"It's always some grift why I need to be … I'm like, 'Man, you do not need thousand-dollar shoes!' He's like, 'We have the money.' I'm like, 'I have the money, you're broke!'" Affleck quipped.

Affleck co-parents his three children with Garner, whom he was married to from 2005 to 2018. During an April 2025 appearance on "Today with Jenna & Friends," Affleck explained how he was teaching his children that they shouldn't expect handouts from their famous parents.
Affleck explained that he wants his children to understand the value of hard work.
The actor said that his children don't care about his success in Hollywood. (Reuters)

"You love your kids. You want to give them everything and do everything for them, but I think you definitely do them a disservice by not connecting [if] you want something that you want, you have to work for that," he said.
During a recent appearance on "Late Night with Seth Meyers," Affleck said that his children don't care about his Hollywood success.

"I remember when my daughter was born, right around the time I directed my first movie and I had a bunch of movies that didn't work and was very uncool and felt kind of despised and thought like, 'God, I really want to make my kids proud with my career,'" he recalled.
"And as I've gotten older, my kids have gotten older, what I realized is, they don't give a s---," he continued as the audience laughed.
"They really don't care," he added. "The most cool thing I've ever done, in my kids' eyes, is, like, become a meme."

In December 2020, Affleck was photographed struggling to carry several Dunkin' iced coffees and a box of Munchkins outside his Los Angeles home. The photos went viral and inspired memes, with social media users joking that Affleck's exasperated expression summed up the frustrations of 2020.

Affleck said that his children were more impressed by his Dunkin' Donuts meme. (Brigette Buckner/Dunkin' via AP)
Affleck later entered into an official partnership with the coffee chain in 2023, when he starred in and directed its first-ever Super Bowl commercial.
During the interview with Meyers, Affleck recalled asking his children why they were impressed by his Dunkin' meme.
"I'm like, 'Why is that cool? Like, because I'm spilling a coffee?'" he recalled. "They're like, 'You're relevant.'"

"I'm like, 'I'm relevant for being this beleaguered, depressed man,'" Affleck quipped.

title: Sarah Ferguson rejects tell-all speculation as expert says discretion is ‘only hope’ for future with family
summary: Royal experts weigh in on Sarah Ferguson's denied memoir rumors, warning a tell-all could risk her relationship with daughters and grandchildren.
story: Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner discusses Sarah Ferguson's denial of tell-all rumors and the potential consequences for daughters Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie.
Sarah Ferguson is setting the record straight about her intent to write a memoir.

In a statement to People, representatives for the former Duchess of York shut down claims she is gearing up to release a tell-all, telling the outlet there have been "no discussions" about a book deal.
"She is not writing a personal memoir," they said.

Rumors she was preparing to release a memoir started in late September, when The Sun reported Ferguson was "days away" from signing a lucrative book deal which would cover her ex-husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein.
Representatives for Ferguson shut down rumors she is preparing to write a tell-all memoir. (Daniele Venturelli/Getty Images)
FORMER PRINCE ANDREW, SARAH FERGUSON DUBBED ROYAL FAMILY’S ‘BONNIE AND CLYDE’ AS EPSTEIN FALLOUT GROWS: AUTHOR

"The other day it was announced by the Sun newspaper that Sarah Ferguson was attempting to write a book, an all-tell book, giving all the secrets away about the royal family. It was strongly denied very quickly by her PR team," royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital.

"And I think the reality was this might have been a strategy to actually gain more initiatives, but who knows? We will never know with the royal family itself. She's obviously very considerate about what might happen if a book was written like this to Eugenie and Beatrice, and also to her former husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor too."

Former Prince Andrew is seen departing Westminster Abbey after the coronation ceremony of King Charles III and Queen Camilla on May 6, 2023, in London, England. The former Duke of York vacated Royal Lodge on Feb. 2, 2026. (Karwai Tang/WireImage/Getty Images)

Turner added that the book would likely not be very complimentary of Windsor, noting that she wasn't "very well treated in the formative years of her marriage with Andrew" and likely felt "lonely" and "isolated."
WATCH: SARAH FERGUSON DENIES TELL-ALL BOOK AMID ROYAL FAMILY CONCERNS: EXPERT

British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that Ferguson is "already persona-non-grata in aristocratic circles" and will be "weary" of making any decisions that will "put her daughters and grandchildren at risk of being ousted completely from the royal family."

"Sarah should simply stick to anything unrelated to the royals, her fiction & anything else without any royal proximity," Fordwich said. "But simply refraining from such wouldn’t be rehabilitation or societal acceptance. Currently, she is persona non grata."

"The only hope she has of any future, indeed also any future with her own daughters and grandchildren, is to be discreet, which is not one of her strongest virtues, to say the least. But staying out of the U.K. for the last seven months was wise to at least let things die down. But despicable behavior will never be forgotten," Fordwich added.
Royal expert, Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that Ferguson is "persona non grata" in the U.K. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

Fordwich added that while a tell-all "would be just a quick fix for her financial woes," it would also "pretty much guarantee zero relationship with her children, grandchildren as well as her social set."

Ferguson spent seven months abroad before announcing her return to the U.K. in August, a decision Fordwich called "wise" as it allowed time for things to "die down," but added, "despicable behavior will never be forgotten."

"Sarah Ferguson is back in the U.K., keeping a low profile and plotting her next move," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "Her chequered past has led to her immense highs and lows over the years. She believes that her current situation is merely another storm in a teacup. She plans to pivot yet again and bounce back."
The controversy surrounding Ferguson stems from her association with Epstein. In the Epstein files, emails allegedly show the former royal asking the child sex offender for financial help.

"Yes, Sarah has done some things wrong in her life, but I think as well, she has got a kind heart," Turner said. "She really is the type of person who will give people anything that they want, and that's partly being her downfall, as she gives very expensive gifts to her friends."

He added: "But I think right now she needs to be looked at as someone who needs help, care, and respect. She is the type of lady that really the queen actually liked in a lot of ways, and she came back into the royal fold. title: Ella Langley says canceled concert was ‘not worth a human life’ after bomb threat
summary: Ella Langley became emotional during her Texas concert explaining why she canceled her sold-out BOK Center show despite Tulsa police finding no credible threat.
story: Country music superstar Ella Langley encouraged fans to not to measure themselves against social media or other people’s expectations during a concert performance.
Ella Langley is speaking out about her decision to cancel her concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma, following a reported bomb threat.
The 27-year-old country star addressed the cancellation while performing in Lubbock, Texas, one day after calling off her sold-out Friday night show at Tulsa's BOK Center.
Langley became emotional while explaining why she decided not to perform despite police finding no credible threat.
MEGAN MORONEY CANCELS SHOW MID-PERFORMANCE, LEAVES STAGE IN TEARS

"I was put in charge of a decision for 15,000 people and I decided to make the decision that I could live with the rest of my life," the "Choosin' Texas" hitmaker told the crowd on Saturday night at the United Supermarkets Arena, according to Taste of Country.
Ella Langley is standing by her decision to cancel her Friday night concert in Oklahoma after a bomb threat.  (FilmMagic)

"Because when it comes to keeping you safe and making sure that this show is a safe place for us to come and enjoy our music, then it will happen," she continued. "But the second, it feels like it's not, I'm not doing it. I'm not doing it because a concert's not worth a human life. It's not."
ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT
"And so I would have made yesterday's decision ten billion times over," she added. "And I'd do it tomorrow and I'd do it the next day."
Langley went on to explain that the safety of her fans outweighed her desire to perform.
The country star said that a concert is "not worth a human life." (Getty Images for SiriusXM)

"Because while I'm grateful to get to do what I do, it's not the most important thing in this life," she said. "What's the most important thing in this life is the people around you that love you and that are there for you no matter what."
"The most important thing in this life is that you wake up every day and feel like, 'You know what, I'm good today. I am so grateful to have woken up today,'" Langley continued.
ELLA LANGLEY DELIVERS POWERFUL FAITH MESSAGE TO CROWD DURING MORGAN WALLEN CONCERT IN CHICAGO
"The most important thing in this life, number one, is your relationship with Jesus Christ," she added.

Langley admitted that she nearly canceled Saturday's concert in Texas because she was still shaken by the incident. However, she credited her faith in Jesus with giving her the courage to return to the stage.
ELLA LANGLEY GOES VIRAL WITH PASSIONATE COMMENTS ABOUT HER CHRISTIAN FAITH, GOD, LOVE AND RELIGION
"If it wasn't for Him," I would have canceled this show tonight," she told the crowd. "I would have."

"But I felt this calling and this tug in my chest saying, 'It's OK. We are safe. We can do this show,'" Langley continued. "And I decided to do it because of Him right there. And that's the only reason."
Langley shared that she almost canceled her Saturday night concert due to the scare.  (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
ELLA LANGLEY'S FAITH AND AUTHENTICITY FUEL RECORD-BREAKING RISE, EXPERTS SAY

"I'm not gonna live in fear," Langley added. "We're going to put on music and get to do this for the rest of our lives. And I know that. I know because this is my calling. This is the thing that I was called to do, and I'm going to continue doing it. Nobody is going to take me out of it or scare me out."
Langley expressed her gratitude to her fans for coming to her Texas show despite the frightening incident at the Oklahoma concert.

"I know yesterday was scary, it was scary for all of us," she said. "But we're just so grateful to be playing this show tonight. We're so grateful and we will never take this for granted. We love it, we love what we do. I wouldn't trade it for the world."

"Tonight I can tell that y'all knew that I've needed what you've given me. And this band and this crew — you knew that we needed this show tonight, so thank you so much for giving it to us," Langley added.
ED SHEERAN'S GILLETTE STADIUM CONCERTS CALLED OFF AS TROUBLED TOUR FACES FRESH SETBACK
Langley announced the cancelation of Friday night's concert on Instagram approximately two hours before the show was scheduled to begin.
Langley announced the cancellation two hours before the show was set to begin.  (Getty Images)

"Due to a serious security threat involving the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team, the incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show. This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team," the singer began.
She said the decision followed guidance from local authorities, venue officials and her security team, adding that she refused to put anyone in danger.

"I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am. This is not a decision that was made lightly. I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way," the country music star's statement concluded.

The BOK Center also released a statement on Friday. "The safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed. We understand the disappointment this news brings and apologize to fans who planned to attend. The safety of fans is our foremost concern and will always come first," the statement read.
The official Instagram account for the BOK Center said that ticket refunds and additional information will be shared as soon as possible.
Tulsa police said that they swept the venue again after a call threatening gunfire and bombs.  (John Schearer)
Langley's explanation for her decision to cancel the concert comes after the Tulsa Police Department said that they found no credible threat to the event.

In a since-deleted statement posted to Facebook, the department explained that officers had conducted routine security sweeps before the concert using K-9 units, bomb technicians, patrol officers and venue security personnel and "did not find anything" dangerous.

"A call was made threatening the lives of people attending the event," they continued. "Out of an abundance of caution, we swept the building and surrounding area and again found no credible threat to the event's safety. We advised the performer's staff that we found no credible threat to the event, but they decided to cancel the performance anyway."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Tulsa Police Department Capt. Richard Meulenberg provided additional details in a video posted to Facebook that has since been deleted. Meulenberg said that after the first security sweeps, "the event was ready to go," according to Saving Country Music.

"And then what happened was a call came in, saying that someone was going to [do] great harm to the people here at this event in the way of shots fired and bombs. So we came out again in an overabundance of caution, used our bomb dogs again, searched the entire area, we could not find a credible threat here at the BOK Center," he said. "We apologize to everyone who came down to the Tulsa area for this. But everything is safe."
Langley is currently on her The Dandelion Tour.  (Terry Wyatt/WireImage via Getty Images)
In an interview with Tulsa news station Fox23, Meulenberg also emphasized that the department did not recommend canceling the concert.

We could not find anything that would make that a credible threat. We advised the group here that was supposed to perform that we could not find a credible threat. We never advised them they should not continue to have their event. They made the decision upon themselves to cancel the event even though we could not find a credible threat."

A spokesperson later told "Good Morning America" that the incident remains under investigation, with the FBI assisting.

title: Ben Affleck says political 'hypocrisy, corruption and failure' left him 'disillusioned'
summary: Ben Affleck calls U.S. politics "terrible" and "tawdry" while promoting "Animals," a new movie in which he plays an L.A. mayoral candidate.
story: Kurt ‘CyberGuy’ Knutsson discusses how AI may impact Hollywood productions on ‘Fox & Friends.’
Ben Affleck has no interest in running for public office.
The "Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice" star told Variety that trying to become a politician sounds "terrible" and "tawdry" to him.

"I just think that’s enormously — I don’t know, man, that seems terrible," Affleck told the outlet while promoting a new movie in which he plays a candidate for L.A. mayor. "There’s a reason why political stories are often chosen as parables for moral compromise. You really get thrust up into the contrast between the ideal version of us and how we should be in our lives and the way it is."
BEN AFFLECK DIRECTS, STARS IN NETFLIX KIDNAPPING THRILLER 'ANIMALS' COMING THIS OCTOBER
Ben Affleck said he has no interest in running for public office. (Getty Images)
The 54-year-old called politics a "very depressing world, in my opinion. Tawdry. And that has no appeal to me."
He also declined to tell the outlet who he was backing for mayor in Los Angeles this November.
"I haven’t thought about being asked that. I don’t know if, given this movie, my endorsement harms or helps anybody," he admitted. "I should stay agnostic, at least until the movie comes out."

Affleck told Good Morning America on Wednesday that he believes the "collective bar for politics because of the way the political world has sort of evolved has gotten so low that there’s this kind of like, you know, people are just sort of looking for like just ‘Somebody shoot me straight.’’"

Playing a man running for mayor taught him: "This is not all that much fun. And it would be a hard way — you’re just raising money all the time."
NETFLIX DROPS FULL TRAILER FOR BEN AFFLECK'S 'ANIMALS' AND EXPECTATIONS ARE ALREADY SOARING
Ben Affleck plays a man running for mayor of Los Angeles in "Animals." (Getty Images)

He said that he and the man playing his campaign manager in the movie decided one day to take campaign shirts and hats with the name of his character, go out in L.A. and claim he was running for mayor.

When he told people he was running as his character, Affleck said voters would ask for a selfie, they seemed interested and "people would launch into their whole thing and I was like ‘If I’m not careful, I’m going to win this.'"
MICHAEL RAPAPORT DOUBLES DOWN ON 2029 NYC MAYORAL RUN, VOWS 'STREET FIGHT' AGAINST ZOHRAN MAMDANI
"Do not vote for me for mayor!" he joked to the camera.

Affleck called holding office an "awful job" in an interview with USA Today via The Sacramento Bee this week, adding that he’s "so disillusioned with the system and with politics and politicians, and the way it works."

When told his campaign ad in the movie was good, he answered, "I'd be flattered, except I think there's such a low bar in politics these days."
Affleck explained that his movie "Animals" is about the moral compromises people make.
Ben Affleck supports then-candidate Barack Obama at an event in 2006. (WireImage)

"The extremely effective nature of when a person individually has something to lose is when they're most apt to make compromises," he says. And there's another part of us, our sort of higher selves, which says, 'Well, I'm going to adhere this moral code even if there's a cost to me.'"

But he said he’s now "averse" to the idea because he’s seen so much "hypocrisy, corruption and failure."

"The way it's constructed now is so geared around money, sound bites, cruelties and gotchas, and little snarky things that really have nothing to do with people's lives whatsoever," he said. "And increasingly, it's easier to get votes appealing to the worst in people than it is appealing to the best in them. If you're telling a story about kind of morality and compromise, there are lots of pressures that are constantly asking you to sacrifice your principles."
Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

title: 10 health conditions may be linked to Alzheimer's, years before diagnosis
summary: Depression, vertigo, headaches and stroke were among conditions linked to early-onset Alzheimer's disease years before diagnosis, a Finnish study suggests.
story: Dr. Jeremy Koppel explains the breakthrough blood test for Alzheimer's disease, detailing how it identifies abnormal protein accumulation. He clarifies the test's current role in diagnosing symptomatic individuals.
Certain medical conditions may signal early-onset Alzheimer’s disease several years before diagnosis, a new Finnish study suggests.
Researchers found that depression, vertigo, headaches and other conditions were more common during the five years preceding diagnosis, potentially offering clues for earlier detection.

The researchers analyzed medical records from 407 people with early-onset Alzheimer’s disease and 4,035 people of similar age and sex without the diagnosis, focusing on the 15 years prior to diagnosis.
SUBTLE CHANGE IN HOW YOU SPEAK COULD BE EARLY SIGN OF DEMENTIA RISK, NEW RESEARCH SUGGESTS
The average age at diagnosis was 60. Early-onset disease is diagnosed in people under 65.
The findings were published in the journal Alzheimer’s & Dementia.
Certain medical conditions may signal early-onset Alzheimer’s disease several years before diagnosis, a new Finnish study suggests. (iStock)
The following conditions were found to be significantly more prevalent among those who were ultimately diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s.
DEMENTIA RISK MORE THAN QUADRUPLES AMONG ADULTS WITH COMMON DISORDER
Vertigo (5.9% of those with diagnosis, vs. 2.1% of those who were not diagnosed)
Depression (5.7% vs. 2.3%)
Headache (4.9% vs. 1.6%)
Stroke (4.4% vs. 2.0%)
Alcohol-related disorders (3.4% vs. 1.4%)
Brain disorders (2.9% vs. 0.9%)
Thyroid disorders (2.5% vs. 0.8%)
Epilepsy (2.2% vs. 0.7%)
Delirium (1.5% vs. 0.1%)
Ear, nose, and throat disorders (5.2% vs. 2.9%)
Researchers found that depression, vertigo, headaches and other conditions were more common during the five years preceding diagnosis. (iStock)
Differences in medical conditions were most pronounced in the five years before an early-onset Alzheimer's diagnosis, the study showed.
3 THINGS TO AVOID IN MIDDLE AGE COULD MEAN 13 MORE YEARS WITHOUT DEMENTIA, STUDY FINDS

The researchers also found that healthcare visits increased substantially among early-onset Alzheimer’s patients immediately before and during the time of diagnosis, which may indicate emerging symptoms.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"It is well-known that the neuropathological changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease begin at least 15 to 20 years before clinical cognitive symptoms appear," Suvi-Johanna Krüger, M.D., Ph.D., study co-author and clinical lecturer at University of Oulu, said in a press release.
"Most previous studies have focused on late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, and considerably less is known about early-onset Alzheimer’s disease."

The researchers analyzed medical records from 407 people with early-onset Alzheimer’s disease and 4,035 people of similar age and sex without the diagnosis, focusing on the 15 years prior to diagnosis. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci, File)
Study limitations
Because the study was observational, it only establishes associations and cannot demonstrate that these conditions can reliably predict Alzheimer's disease.
"Our study cannot determine whether these conditions cause early-onset Alzheimer’s disease or whether they are consequences of the underlying disease process," Krüger noted.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"Some conditions may represent risk factors, while others may reflect early symptoms or changes occurring during the prodromal phase of the disease."
It is also possible that genetics, lifestyle and socioeconomic factors played a role in the patients’ outcomes.
"Early diagnosis is important because more treatment and support options are available in the early stages of the disease."
Also, the researchers could not independently verify all medical diagnoses or assess the severity of the patients’ disease. Additionally, the findings may not apply to populations outside Finland.

Larger studies looking at disease biomarkers, genetics and clinical assessments could help determine whether there is a casual relationship between the medical conditions and Alzheimer’s incidence and whether these medical patterns could be used to improve early detection.

For people experiencing any persistent medical symptoms, including issues with memory or cognition, experts say it’s important to see a healthcare provider.

"Early diagnosis is important because more treatment and support options are available in the early stages of the disease," Krüger advised.
"Early diagnosis also gives individuals and their families more time to plan for the future and access appropriate support services."

title: Selma Blair's lawyer cites missed medication, head injury after in-flight arrest: What doctors say
summary: Selma Blair's attorney claims she missed doses of a powerful MS medication, triggering severe neurological symptoms before her in-flight arrest.
story: Dr. Lee Murray, a board-certified neurologist practicing in Jackson, Tennessee, shared the potential health effects that could occur if a multiple sclerosis patient skips doses of necessary medications.
Selma Blair’s recent in-flight arrest has raised questions about the potential effects when a person with multiple sclerosis misses prescribed medication.

The actress, 54, was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault after allegedly attacking a police officer and nurse following an altercation with flight attendants aboard a Delta flight into New York City, The Associated Press reported.
In court, Blair’s attorney, Shawn Barnes, said that Blair had missed several doses of Nuedexta, "a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms," according to multiple outlets.
SELMA BLAIR ACCUSED OF KICKING NURSE HOURS AFTER JFK PLANE ARREST

The attorney added that Blair hit her head during the flight, which departed from Los Angeles, and was in "a state of severe confusion and disorientation." He also suggested the altitude may have been a factor.
The incident was the result of a "medical emergency" and not criminal misconduct, he claimed.
Selma Blair’s recent in-flight arrest has raised questions about the potential effects when a person with multiple sclerosis misses prescribed medication. (Getty Images)
Blair was diagnosed with MS in 2018.
Fox News Digital reached out to Blair's representatives requesting comment.
What to know about MS medications
There are three primary treatment approaches for multiple sclerosis, according to Dr. Lee Murray, a board-certified neurologist practicing in Jackson, Tennessee, at West Tennessee Healthcare.
"The first-line treatments we utilize try to prevent recurrent inflammatory attacks," Murray, who has not treated Blair, told Fox News Digital.
'HELICOPTER BRAIN' COULD BE MAKING YOU FEEL SICK: HOW TO SPOT IT AND WHAT TO DO
These medications often involve IV infusions, but they can be in the form of pills or injections the patient gives themselves.
"These are oftentimes medications folks take for several years," Murray said. "The hope of that is to keep the MS suppressed, to keep [the patient] from having MS attacks."

Selma Blair exits Queens Criminal Court on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026. The actress was arrested Sunday after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)
When patients experience an MS relapse, doctors may prescribe high-dose steroids, either orally or intravenously, to reduce inflammation and help speed recovery, according to Cleveland Clinic.
Patients with multiple sclerosis often have other health issues, Murray noted.
"If an MS medication dosage is missed, the patient runs the risk of having an MS relapse."

"For instance, patients with MS may have bladder difficulties, or they’ll develop depression or neuropathic pain," he said. "And so we prescribe medications that don't treat the MS itself, but they deal with the symptoms related to MS."
Dr. Yoshua Quinones, board-certified internist with Medical Offices of Manhattan, reiterated that there are different classes of MS medications.
PARKINSON'S PATIENTS MAY PROTECT MEMORY AND MOVEMENT WITH ONE SIMPLE HABIT
"Disease-modifying therapy reduces relapses, new MRI lesions and long-term disability accumulation," Quinones, who also did not treat Blair, told Fox News Digital.
Other medications are used to treat acute relapses or manage symptoms such as fatigue, walking difficulties, spasticity and bladder problems.
Actress Selma Blair and her son Arthur Saint Bleick attend the 26th annual Race to Erase MS Gala at the Beverly Hilton hotel on May 10, 2019, in Beverly Hills. (Getty Images)
Disease-modifying therapies themselves fall into several categories, according to the doctor.

Immunomodulators help regulate the immune system, while anti-trafficking drugs prevent certain immune cells from reaching the brain and spinal cord. Cell-depleting therapies, which are generally considered highly effective treatments, target and remove specific immune cells.
Risks of skipping doses
It’s essential for patients to be compliant with their MS medications, according to Murray.

"If an MS medication dosage is missed, the patient runs the risk of having an MS relapse, which can result in acute or new changes neurologically," he said. "There's a host of different symptoms that can occur."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Potential effects of a relapse may include balance difficulties, vision loss, dizziness, bowel or bladder dysfunction, or weakness, numbness or tingling on one side.

In Blair's case, Murray said, "If the Nuedexta was being used to treat pseudobulbar palsy secondary to her MS, missed doses could result in uncontrolled crying or laughter and emotional lability (rapid or unpredictable changes in emotion or mood)."
"I have never seen a missed dose of Nuedexta cause physical aggression," he added.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

If a patient with multiple sclerosis has missed doses of medication and begins to develop new neurological deficits, they should seek medical attention to determine whether they are in an active MS flare, the neurologist advised.
"Recognizing that and being able to quickly get on high-dose steroids can reverse some of the symptoms the patient may be experiencing," he said.
It’s essential for patients to be compliant with their MS medications, according to a neurologist. (iStock)
Although steroids can speed recovery from an MS relapse, they have not been shown to improve long-term outcomes, according to the MS Society.
Quinones agreed that skipping medications will reduce disease control.

"Poor compliance will increase the risk of relapse and MS-related hospitalizations," he said. "For example, if you stop any anti-trafficking medication, it carries a high risk of rapid disease reactivation. Abrupt cessation of this class can even trigger a rebound worse than baseline."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Cell-depleting agents can act over months, so a single missed or delayed dose is less immediately impactful, Quinones added.
"A single dose of disease-modifying therapy is not catastrophic — however, if constantly missed, it can raise a relapse risk."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The risks of missing medication depend on the specific drug, how long treatment is interrupted and the patient's individual circumstances, according to doctors.
Fox News’ Tracy Wright contributed reporting.

title: Popular erectile dysfunction pill may deliver additional boost to aging men
summary: Tadalafil boosted muscle precursor cell survival in a lab study, but researchers say the active Cialis ingredient also delayed mature muscle development.
story: Jacob Zemer, a New York-based fitness coach who primarily trains clients ranging from 35 to 55 years old, said there are several reasons adults start losing muscle as they get older.
Researchers in Italy have discovered a potential association between the common erectile dysfunction drug Cialis (tadalafil) and muscle regeneration.
The study, published in the journal Molecular Biology Reports, tested the drug on mouse muscle cells in a laboratory.
Over a seven-day period, the researchers looked at how the drug affected muscle cell growth, survival and development.
VIAGRA COULD DO MORE THAN ADVERTISED AS STUDY REVEALS SURPRISING HEALTH SUPERPOWER
Tadalafil was found to increase the number of muscle precursor cells, which are involved in the early stages of muscle formation, and helped more of them survive.
The drug also showed signs of helping muscles repair themselves by encouraging growth and reducing cell death.
Researchers in Italy have discovered a potential association between the common erectile dysfunction drug Cialis (tadalafil) and muscle regeneration. (iStock)
Despite these positive outcomes, the research found that tadalafil delayed the development of fully mature muscle cells.
This suggests that the drug could create and maintain more cells involved in muscle regeneration but does not indicate an increase in muscle size and function in humans.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
Because the study was conducted in mouse models, the results may differ when applied to humans, posing a limitation to the study findings.
The study lasted just seven days, so more research is needed to understand the drug's long-term effects, the researchers acknowledged.
"This research opens up exciting new possibilities for future therapeutic strategies in muscle recovery," a researcher commented. (iStock)

Study co-author Dr. Cristina Antinozzi, a researcher in the Endocrinology Unit at the University of Rome Foro Italico, said these findings represent an "encouraging look at how tadalafil might be repurposed to support muscle tissue repair and regeneration."
"That's a fascinating biological signal, but it's far from proving that Cialis builds muscle or improves recovery in people."

"While more work is needed, this research opens up exciting new possibilities for future therapeutic strategies in muscle recovery, though it also highlights the need to monitor how such mechanisms might be viewed or misused in sports and performance contexts," she told Fox News Digital.
Dr. Kien Vuu, a radiologist and founder of VuuMD Performance and Longevity in Los Angeles, who was not involved in the study, agreed that this is an "intriguing early finding."
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"In mouse muscle cells studied in a laboratory, tadalafil — the active ingredient in Cialis — helped muscle precursor cells grow and survive, but also delayed their maturation into muscle fibers," he told Fox News Digital.
"That's a fascinating biological signal, but it's far from proving that Cialis builds muscle or improves recovery in people.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"Successful regeneration ultimately requires those cells to mature and form functional muscle tissue. This experiment didn't establish that outcome."
Vuu said this is "worth studying" from a longevity perspective because age-related muscle loss contributes "significantly" to frailty, metabolic dysfunction and loss of independence.
Resistance training, adequate protein and quality sleep remain the "most reliable ways" to protect muscle with age, an expert says. (iStock)

"However, this was a laboratory cell study, not a clinical trial," he said. "We need animal studies and eventually human trials examining actual muscle mass, strength, physical function and safety before drawing conclusions about clinical use."
Lifestyle practices such as resistance training, adequate protein and quality sleep remain the "most reliable ways" to protect muscle with age, Vuu added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The expert noted that tadalafil also carries "meaningful risks," including dangerous blood pressure reductions when combined with nitrates.
"So, people should not take it for muscle-building based on these findings," he said.
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Doctors may be getting childhood obesity wrong, new research suggests
summary: A Lancet Commission definition of clinical obesity cuts pediatric rates sharply by requiring evidence of health complications beyond body mass index.
story: Murdoch Children's Research Insitute pediatrician Dr. Danielle Longmore discusses a new global childhood obesity definition from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute that looks beyond BMI. Longmore explains how the new definition considers critical health impacts.
A new global definition of childhood obesity is reframing how doctors evaluate youth health, looking past traditional body mass index (BMI) measurements to focus on actual physiological impacts.

According to research from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute in Australia, just 2.1% to 4.9% of children and adolescents qualify as clinically obese under the revised standard, compared to 7% to 10.8% under standard BMI calculations.
Dr. Danielle Longmore, a pediatrician at the Melbourne institute, outlined the shift during an appearance on "Fox & Friends."
YOUR WAISTLINE COULD REVEAL A HIDDEN HEART RISK YOUR BMI MISSES, MAJOR STUDY FINDS

"There's a push to really understand the impact of body fat on health," Longmore said. "BMI is really just measuring size. So, it doesn't really have a way of capturing whether somebody is well or unwell."
The traditional BMI measurement calculates a person's weight relative to their height.
While clinical obesity rates are substantially lower in youth, they surge with age, peaking at 52% among adults aged 65 to 74 as chronic conditions accumulate. (iStock)

The new definition, developed by an international panel of medical experts convened by the medical journal The Lancet, requires evidence of both excess body fat and related health problems or limitations in daily activities.
WEIGHT GAIN IN CERTAIN DECADE OF LIFE MAY BE MORE DANGEROUS, STUDY SUGGESTS
These indicators can range from elevated blood pressure and abnormal blood sugar to impaired mobility or poor sleep.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Longmore noted that many children defined as obese by BMI metrics are active, sleeping well, attending school and otherwise healthy.
The new diagnostic model formalizes what many pediatricians already practice by assessing blood pressure, blood sugar, sleep and physical mobility alongside size. (iStock)

"I think this definition just really clarifies what people have been doing in actual clinical practice," Longmore said, noting that physicians typically evaluate patients for underlying complications rather than relying strictly on scale weight.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
While clinical obesity appears to be significantly less prevalent in youth under the new model, the trajectory reverses dramatically later in life.
The study, which analyzed nearly 800,000 individuals across their lifespan, found that clinical obesity rates climbed through adulthood.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Among adults ages 65 to 74, the rate of clinical obesity reached 52%, as health problems linked to excess body fat became more common with age.
The findings come at a time when prescription weight loss medications, particularly GLP-1 receptor agonists, are gaining in popularity.
Many children categorized as obese by traditional BMI standards are fit, active and otherwise healthy, without secondary medical complications. (iStock)
However, Longmore cautioned that the study's dataset reflects pre-GLP-1 records, making the long-term impact of these treatments an open area for future study.

"This is really just the start of understanding what this new diagnostic entity means, and we really need more research," Longmore said, emphasizing that while the definition refines clinical diagnoses, early health interventions and lifestyle prevention remain critical for children at risk.

title: Biggest waste of money in your home gym may surprise you, fitness expert says
summary: Fitness coach Jacob Zemer reveals the three home gym essentials — bands, dumbbells and a bench — that let you train every muscle group on a budget.
story: New York-based fitness coach Jacob Zemer spoke with Fox News Digital about the most worthwhile investments for working out at home — and which equipment may not deliver enough bang for the buck.
Americans are spending more on health and wellness, research shows — and for some home gym enthusiasts, the cost can quickly climb into the thousands.
A YouGov poll conducted in September 2026 found that 31% of Americans are spending more on health and wellness than a year ago, while 20% expect to spend more in the coming year.
Meanwhile, a 2026 poll by Garage Gym Experiment, an online community for home fitness enthusiasts, found that 44% of respondents expected to spend at least $1,000 on their home gyms this year.
FITNESS EXPERT REVEALS 6 THINGS PEOPLE OVER 35 SHOULD DO AFTER WORKOUTS TO STAY STRONG
But building an effective home gym doesn’t have to break the bank, according to New York-based fitness coach Jacob Zemer.
The biggest home gym money-waster may not be a particular piece of equipment, he said, but rather anything that takes up significant space and is difficult to set up or use consistently.
Building an effective home gym doesn’t have to break the bank, according to New York-based fitness coach Jacob Zemer, right. (Jacob Zemer)
Zemer spoke with Fox News Digital about the most worthwhile investments for working out at home — and which equipment may not deliver enough bang for the buck.
The 3 home gym essentials
"A lot of people think building a home gym requires an elaborate setup, and it doesn't," Zemer said.
If someone is building a home gym from scratch, the fitness pro recommends starting with a few affordable pieces and adding equipment over time.
10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG
"You can accomplish everything for every muscle group with just three items," he said.
Exercise bands are a good first investment, Zemer said, "just because they're so incredibly affordable."
They’re also very effective, he said, especially for those who are new to strength training.
Exercise bands are a good first investment, Zemer said, "just because they're so incredibly affordable." (Jacob Zemer)
"You can do everything you need to with just those pieces of equipment — and you can travel with them, bring them on a plane and to a hotel, which makes them very versatile," Zemer said.
When choosing dumbbells, it’s important to consider how much floor space they’ll take up — especially if the home gym is in a room with multiple purposes, according to Zemer.
"With adjustable dumbbells, you can have a very small floor print — however, they are a little bit more costly, and some of them are slightly fragile, so just be mindful of that," he advised.
4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS
Beginners should first focus on learning the proper form and choosing a weight that makes the final repetitions challenging, according to Zemer.
Progress doesn’t always mean moving to heavier dumbbells, he noted.
When choosing dumbbells, it’s important to consider how much floor space they’ll take up — especially if the home gym is in a room with multiple purposes, according to Zemer. (Jacob Zemer)
"Pushing yourself doesn’t mean adding 20 pounds — it could mean doing one more rep," Zemer said. "You need to progressively get stronger, because your body will adapt to the stimulus you’re using."
Once it becomes easy to complete a high number of repetitions, it may be time to increase the weight.
With some exercises, it can be limiting if you have to lie on the floor or stand, Zemer said.
"You can get quite an affordable bench online," he said. "I would look for one that both declines and inclines, maybe even perhaps sits completely upright. That will give you a lot of versatility."
For added versatility, Zemer suggests looking for a bench that both declines and inclines, and maybe even sits completely upright. (Jacob Zemer)
The biggest waste: equipment you won’t use
Before buying a piece of home gym equipment, Zemer recommends considering how much space it requires, how many exercises it supports and whether it will be easy to use consistently.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Equipment that is bulky or difficult to move, or requires too much setup, may end up becoming an expensive waste of money.
"The most important thing is that it’s quick and easy to set up, easy to grab and therefore more likely to be used," he said. "The more setup it requires, the less likely you will to be use it."
Before buying a piece of home gym equipment, Zemer recommends considering how much space it requires, how many exercises it supports and whether it will be easy to use consistently. (Jacob Zemer)

Zemer learned that lesson after buying lever arms, attachments that connect to a power rack and move up and down for exercises such as presses, rows and squats. Because the equipment was cumbersome to move, he eventually sold it secondhand.
"The secondhand market of gym equipment is brutal, so if you buy something, and you don't use it, the resale value is next to none," Zemer cautioned.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
He recommends prioritizing items that serve multiple purposes, rather than devices designed to target just one body part.
"I always look for equipment that can do multiple things," he said.
"A lot of people think building a home gym requires an elaborate setup, and it doesn't."
Do you need cardio equipment?
Cardio equipment is not essential for everyone, according to the trainer, especially for those who are mobile.
Many people can also raise their heart rate through activities such as walking, running or strength-training workouts performed at a faster pace, he said.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For those who prefer a cardio machine, Zemer recommends choosing an option that is versatile and less likely to aggravate the knees or back, such as a stationary bike or ski erg (an indoor exercise machine that simulates the motion of cross-country skiing).
