title: France is devouring itself as school riots reveal a crisis far bigger than broken classrooms
summary: Student protests in France over crumbling schools expose deep tensions as Jean-Luc Mélenchon's La France Insoumise allegedly exploits the growing unrest.
story: FDD Special Envoy Simone Rodan-Benzaquen says legitimate student grievances have been hijacked by political movements seeking to fuel unrest and deepen divisions across France.

Student protests over crumbling schools despite billions in public spending are fueling a broader crisis in France, and experts warn that the country's mounting financial troubles, President Emmanuel Macron's weakened political center and radical movements are pushing the unrest far beyond its original educational grievances.

Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, the Foundation for Defense of Democracies' senior envoy for Europe, told Fox News Digital in an interview from Paris that what began in September with legitimate complaints about school conditions has increasingly been exploited by political forces seeking confrontation with the state.
"Overall, I'd say the anger is real, but the violence, I would say, is organized," she said, adding that destroying schools would do nothing to improve the education system.
FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION
A protesting student feeds a burnt barrier during a blockading action outside the secondary school Le Corbusier, in Aubervilliers, northern Paris on Oct. 1, 2026. (Lou Benoist/AFP via Getty Images)

Seventy-two percent of education expenditures went toward salaries, social contributions and pensions for teaching and non-teaching personnel, while just 8.5% went toward investment, including infrastructure and equipment. The figures cover the entire education system, not just high schools, according to France's Education Ministry's 2026 statistical overview.

Harvey Feigenbaum, a professor of political science and international affairs at George Washington University and an expert on French politics, told Fox News Digital that France's underlying problem is a government caught between expensive social commitments, sluggish economic growth and mounting pressure to cut spending.
"France is in deep debt. It wants to cut its expenses," Feigenbaum said, explaining that years of financial pressure and neglected school facilities have fueled frustration among students.

The scale of the financial predicament is striking. According to Eurostat, French public debt stood at 117.6% of GDP in the first quarter of 2026, the third-highest ratio in the European Union, behind Greece and Italy.

Reuters reported Oct. 8 that rising borrowing costs and investor concerns have severely limited the government's ability to resolve unrest through additional spending, a strategy employed during previous waves of French protests.
The financial squeeze has collided with an increasingly fragmented political system, creating opportunities for parties at both ends of the political spectrum to capitalize on public dissatisfaction.
FRENCH SCHOOL RIOTS DEEPEN AS EXPERTS POINT TO FAR-LEFT ALLIANCE FUELING ‘BROADER CONFRONTATION’

Protestors gather around the Monument à la République in Place de la République in Paris on Oct. 4, 2026, during nationwide demonstrations against an overcrowded, ill-equipped and understaffed education system.  (Veronique de Viguerie/Getty Images)
Macron's political center collapses
For Feigenbaum, the long-term roots of the crisis lie in Macron's political legacy.
When Macron won the presidency in 2017, he promised to move beyond France's traditional left-right divide, combining policies from both sides into a new centrist political movement.
But Feigenbaum argues that the strategy produced an unintended consequence, weakening France's established moderate parties without creating a durable governing coalition to replace them.
"What he ended up doing was attracting the moderate voters from the parties of the moderate left and the parties from the moderate right, and essentially destroyed those parties," Feigenbaum said.
He argued that the collapse of the traditional political center helped create space for more ideologically polarized movements.
"Macron is a smart man, but he's a terrible politician," the professor added.

Macron's controversial pension reforms illustrate the difficulty of persuading French voters to accept reductions in longstanding public benefits, Feigenbaum argued. Those efforts triggered widespread protests, while implementation of the 2023 retirement changes has since been suspended until 2028.
The situation became especially difficult after Macron called snap parliamentary elections in 2024, producing a deeply divided National Assembly without a governing majority.
"Even if the government wanted to do something coherent, they simply don't have the votes to do it," Feigenbaum said.
That paralysis has left Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu handling the immediate unrest while Macron faces questions about the stability of the political system he helped reshape.
FRENCH PM REJECTS POLICE BRUTALITY CLAIMS AFTER TEENS SEVERELY INJURED IN PROTESTS: 'ACCIDENTS HAPPEN'

Protesters hold a Palestinian flag Oct. 6, 2026, the day French high school and university students attend a demonstration in Strasbourg as part of a nationwide day of protests and blockades, voicing anger over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages and dilapidated school buildings, which students blame on years of underinvestment. (Reuters/Kai Pfaffenbach)
Why are France's schools struggling despite billions in spending?
The protests began in the Paris suburbs in September amid complaints about overcrowded classrooms, inadequate heating and cooling, aging buildings and teachers who were not replaced when absent.
Rodan-Benzaquen said the anger reflected years of educational instability, frequent ministerial changes and reforms that have failed to resolve persistent school problems.
She also pointed to a broader sense of anxiety among young people about their economic future, artificial intelligence, climate change and international conflicts.

According to the OECD's September 2026 Education at a Glance report, France spent $16,674 in funding per student in general upper secondary education in 2023, compared with an OECD average of $12,421, adjusted for purchasing power.

Anti-riot police officers face protesting students carrying out blockading action outside the secondary school Le Corbusier, in Aubervilliers, northern Paris Oct. 1, 2026. (Lou Benoist/AFP via Getty Images)
Yet teachers and students continue to complain about basic shortages.
Responsibility for public high school buildings and equipment falls to regional authorities, while the national government oversees much of the education system, including teacher staffing.
Feigenbaum said France's centralized education structure makes national leaders the focus of public anger when schools fail to deliver.
The pressure has already forced a concession.
Reuters reported Friday that Education Minister Édouard Geffray announced an emergency plan to deploy 3,000 qualified educators to particularly affected schools, costing several dozen million euros.
Student unions welcomed the measure as an initial victory but pledged to continue demonstrating.

The spending figures raise broader questions about whether France's financial and political priorities have left sufficient resources for maintaining school infrastructure and meeting students' needs. They do not, however, establish that teachers' unions or other organized constituencies have improperly diverted funding.
TEEN'S HAND BLOWN OFF BY POLICE GRENADE DURING FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS: REPORT

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leader of the French left-wing La France Insoumise party, delivers a speech during an electoral campaign meeting of the local LFI candidate for French municipal elections in Marseille, southern France, March 7, 2026. (Miguel Medina/AFP via Getty Images)
How the far left entered the unrest
As the demonstrations expanded, the involvement of France's hard-left La France Insoumise party, known as LFI, led by Jean-Luc Mélenchon, became an increasingly contentious issue.

Reuters reported Oct. 1 that French intelligence agencies had told a government crisis meeting that LFI and affiliated activists played a role in fomenting the unrest. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez also cited agitators moving between schools to encourage violence.
LFI has denied responsibility and accused authorities of aggravating tensions through their response.
Rodan-Benzaquen said far-left movements were capitalizing on students' frustration.
"There is an obvious instrumentalization, obvious manipulation," she said, arguing that activists were seeking to push some protesters toward violence.
She linked the unrest to what she described as Mélenchon's broader political strategy ahead of France's 2027 presidential election.

"His idea is that, on the one hand, he will scare voters on the right and on the far right, who will then go to vote for the far right, and, on the other hand, he would mobilize his own camp," she said.

Rodan-Benzaquen argued that intensifying political confrontation could help Mélenchon consolidate his support among younger voters and immigrant communities, while portraying the far right as an increasingly serious threat.
She described it as a calculated political strategy rather than a spontaneous response to students' concerns.

The involvement of LFI politicians has been documented by French media, although there is disagreement over whether the party helped initiate the demonstrations or became involved after the protests began.

An Oct. 2 investigation by Le Monde examined a police intelligence assessment describing radical left activity around schools in Seine-Saint-Denis but questioned whether the evidence established that the movement itself was politically orchestrated.
Feigenbaum offered a more cautious interpretation, describing some of the violent perpetrators as fringe provocateurs who exploit broader demonstrations without necessarily directing them.
"They're not being organized by some, you know, some mastermind at the national level, at least as far as anyone knows," he said.
FRANCE ROCKED BY STUDENT RIOTS AS HUNDREDS ARRESTED, VIOLENCE SPREADS NATIONWIDE
Protesters hold Palestinian and Antifa flags as French high school and university students attend a demonstration in Strasbourg, France, Thursday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters)
Islamist influence or political solidarity?
The demonstrations have also raised questions about whether Islamist groups and pro-Palestinian activists are seeking to use the unrest to advance broader ideological causes.
Rodan-Benzaquen argued that Mélenchon's emphasis on Gaza and the Palestinian cause has helped bring together political constituencies that might otherwise have little in common.

"It's sort of the idea of sort of an intersection of different movements where they manage to bring together the different groups, the far left, Islamist movements, pro-Palestinian activists," she said.
She pointed to Palestinian flags appearing during the demonstrations as an indication of how the movement has expanded beyond its original educational demands.
The FDD expert argued that Islamist elements were attempting to capitalize on the turmoil, although she cautioned against reducing the entire crisis to immigration or religion.
"But this goes far beyond the issue of immigration. It goes far beyond the issue of Islamism. It goes far beyond the issue of Islam," she said.
EUROPE’S LEFT COURTS MUSLIM VOTERS AS ANTI-ISRAEL POLITICS RESHAPE CONTINENT
Students march with a large red banner reading "Police officers, enemy of the people" during a protest against under-resourced schools in Rennes, France, Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Jeremias Gonzalez/AP)
A crisis France cannot simply spend its way out of
The government's latest concessions have not ended the protests.
According to Reuters on Friday, 141 schools remained closed while students continued demanding broader reforms. Nearly 10% of teaching hours in French public high schools remained unstaffed.
For Rodan-Benzaquen, one of the greatest dangers is that the demonstrations reflect a society increasingly divided into competing political realities.

She described how her 17-year-old son created separate left-wing and right-wing Instagram accounts and encountered radically different portrayals of the same unrest, one emphasizing police violence and the other violence by protesters.
"Now, if you live in two drastically different realities, it is very complicated to come to any form of dialog and end agreement," she said.
Her warning extends beyond France's current protests.
"We are in an extremely polarized environment," Rodan-Benzaquen said, noting that social media can deepen divisions and allow confrontations to escalate rapidly.
Feigenbaum sees an additional structural danger of a government burdened by accumulated financial obligations and deprived of the political consensus needed to reform them.

The result is a country spending heavily to sustain its public institutions while struggling to deliver the services citizens expect and a political system increasingly consumed by conflict over how to fix them.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
French President Emmanuel Macron delivers a speech during the World Economic Forum annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland, Jan. 20, 2026. (Harun Ozalp/Anadolu via Getty Images)

What began as a rebellion against broken classrooms has become a test of whether France can reconcile its costly promises with its financial reality before the divisions consuming its schools deepen further.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Massive 7.7 magnitude earthquake strikes Panama as officials investigate potential tsunami threat
summary: A powerful earthquake struck Panama's southern coast Friday, prompting officials to investigate a possible tsunami threat after the USGS lowered its magnitude estimate from 8.0 to 7.7.
story: Workers gathered in parks and public squares after a powerful earthquake shook buildings in Panama's capital Friday. (Credit: Associated Press)
A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck off Panama's southern coast Friday, shaking the country's capital as officials investigated a potential tsunami threat.

The U.S. Geological Survey initially measured the earthquake at magnitude 8.0 before lowering its estimate to 7.7. The quake struck at 1:56 p.m. ET, at a depth of 7.8 miles, near Pitaloza Arriba, Panama.A 5.5 magnitude aftershock followed, with its epicenter approximately 50 miles east of the initial earthquake.The Panama Canal said operations were continuing normally following Friday's earthquake, with emergency protocols activated and technical teams inspecting facilities for possible damage. Canal officials said their priority was ensuring the safety of workers, vessels, crews and nearby communities as assessments continued.
MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF
People stand outside the maternity ward of the Santo Tomas hospital after a severe magnitude 7.7 earthquake thet hit the country in Panama City Oct. 9, 2026. (Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty Images)
The earthquake was felt in Panama City and in San José, the capital of neighboring Costa Rica, according to Reuters.

Tsunami officials warned that waves reaching 3 to 10 feet above tide levels were possible along some coastal areas of Panama, while parts of Ecuador could experience waves of approximately 1 to 3 feet.
Smaller tsunami waves of less than 1 foot above tide levels were forecast for coastal areas of Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Nicaragua and Peru.
COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION
Medical workers and patients gather outside a hospital after a powerful earthquake in Panama Oct. 9, 2026. (Martin Bernetti/AFP via Getty Images)
Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino said in a series of posts on X that he was visiting areas affected by Friday's earthquake and coordinating emergency assistance with government officials.

Mulino said he had ordered the mobilization of personnel, resources and aid for affected communities, along with structural assessments to determine the extent of the damage. He also thanked neighboring countries for their support and said assistance from the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean (CAF) would go toward helping those affected.
The president said he was traveling through Penonomé with government officials to coordinate relief efforts and thanked the United States and other countries for their offers of assistance.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a Friday post on X that the State Department was rapidly mobilizing resources and personnel to assist Panama at the request of the Panamanian government. Rubio said the U.S. was closely monitoring the earthquake and directed Americans needing assistance to the department's 24-hour consular hotline at +1-202-501-4444 from abroad or +1-888-407-4747 from the U.S. and Canada.

The U.S. Embassy in Panama also said it was assessing potential damage and working to account for the safety and whereabouts of visitors and personnel. In a separate X post, the embassy urged Americans in Panama to enroll in the State Department's Smart Traveler Enrollment Program at STEP.State.gov and follow its social media accounts for updates.
Despite the potential danger to coastal communities near the earthquake, officials said a Pacific-wide tsunami was not expected.
People gather in a Panama City square after evacuating a building after a powerful earthquake. (Arnulfo Franco/AFP via Getty Images)
Earthquakes measuring between 7.0 and 7.9 can cause serious damage, according to Michigan Technological University.CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Information about possible damage or casualties from Friday's earthquake was not immediately available.

title: Who is Navi Pillay? Nobel Peace Prize winner's UN record renews fierce antisemitism accusations
summary: Navi Pillay's 2026 Nobel Peace Prize sparked backlash from Jewish advocacy groups and UN Watch over allegations of anti-Israel bias and antisemitism.
story: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivers a blistering address to the United Nations General Assembly, labeling delegates who walked out of his speech as 'moral cowards.' Senior correspondent Eric Shawn reports on intense anti-Israel protests in New York City, leading to several high-profile activist arrests.

The decision to award the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to former U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay sparked fierce backlash Friday from Jewish advocacy groups and U.N. watchdogs accusing the South African jurist of longstanding anti-Israel bias and defending antisemitic rhetoric.
The Norwegian Nobel Committee honored Pillay, 85, for her contributions to international law and efforts to hold perpetrators of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide accountable.

But her selection immediately reignited controversies surrounding her leadership of U.N. investigations into Israel, her defense of a fellow commissioner accused of antisemitism and positions she expressed before being appointed to investigate the Jewish state.
ICC PROSECUTOR WHOSE NETANYAHU WARRANT FUELED MAMDANI ARREST THREAT IS FIRED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT
South African Judge Navi Pillay speaks during a news conference in Geneva Sept. 16, 2025. (Fabrice Coffrini/AFP via Getty Images)

"Navi Pillay is indeed a world leader, an individual at the forefront of the international spread of the poisonous forms of antisemitism that beset the 21st century," Anne Bayefsky, president of Human Rights Voices and director of the Touro Institute on Human Rights, told Fox News Digital.

Bayefsky accused Pillay of having "perfected the art of perverting legal and universal standards of human rights to demonize and delegitimize Jewish self-determination. This award stands as a testament to human wrongs."

The Nobel Committee offered a sharply different assessment of Pillay's legacy, praising her lifelong commitment to international justice and describing her career as an example of courage and integrity in defending the rule of law.
ISRAEL VINDICATED BY GAZA NUTRITION DATA AFTER ‘BLOOD LIBEL’ STARVATION CLAIMS, UN ENVOY SAYS

Controversial South African judge Navi Pillay, chair of the independent United Nations Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem and Israel arrives to a news conference in Geneva June 18, 2025. (Fabrice Coffrini/AFP via Getty Images.)
Who Is Navi Pillay?

Born in Durban, South Africa, in 1941, Pillay built her career challenging apartheid-era discrimination, becoming the first non-White woman appointed to South Africa's high court. She later served as a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court.

From 2008 to 2014, she served as U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights. In 2021, she was appointed to chair the U.N. Human Rights Council's open-ended Commission of Inquiry investigating alleged violations in Israel and the Palestinian territories.

In September 2025, the commission concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, a finding Israel rejected as politically motivated and biased. The commission's conclusion was not a ruling by an international court.
Geneva-based UN Watch condemned Friday's Nobel announcement, accusing Pillay of breaching the impartiality expected of international investigators.
UN CHIEF BACKS OFFICIAL WHO REPOSTED ANTI-ISRAEL ACTIVIST'S CLAIMS AMID CALLS FOR INVESTIGATION
The flag alley at the United Nations European headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, Sept. 11, 2023. (Denis Balibouse/File Photo/Reuters)

"We are shocked that the Nobel Committee honored Navi Pillay," Executive Director Hillel Neuer said. "Her troubling record on antisemitism and gross breach of ethics in presiding over a notorious U.N. commission utterly disqualifies her from such an award."

Neuer pointed to a June 2020 manifesto that Pillay signed calling on governments to "Sanction Apartheid Israel," along with a June 2021 letter urging President Joe Biden to punish Israel after its conflict with Hamas.
UN Watch argued that the positions raised questions about her impartiality before she accepted the commission's chairmanship in July 2021.

Despite the criticism, U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres congratulated Pillay on receiving the Nobel Peace Prize, praising her decades-long career in international justice and specifically highlighting her leadership of the U.N. investigation into Israel.

"For decades, she has been a champion of international law and human rights and a steadfast, independent voice of justice amidst some of the most historic international legal cases of our time," Guterres said in a statement on Friday.

Guterres highlighted her different roles, including chairing the commission investigating Israel and the Palestinian territories, declaring that Pillay had demonstrated "that the force of law must prevail over the law of force and that defending human rights is the surest safeguard against injustice."
NORWAY FACES BACKLASH OVER 'DEEPLY RACIST' PROPOSAL TO JAIL CITIZENS FOR WEST BANK BUSINESS

A view of the rostrum where the Nobel Committee's chairman, Jørgen Watne Frydnes will announce the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize for 2025, in Oslo Oct. 10, 2025. (Rodrigo Freitas/NTB Scanpix via AP)

Another controversy erupted in 2022 when fellow commissioner Miloon Kothari suggested that social media criticism of the investigation was controlled by the "Jewish lobby" and questioned Israel's U.N. membership.

The remarks were condemned by U.S. officials, including then-State Department antisemitism envoy Deborah Lipstadt. Pillay defended Kothari, arguing his comments had been taken out of context. Kothari subsequently apologized, calling his language inappropriate and insensitive.
The controversy also reached Germany, where Berlin's mayor withdrew support for a planned event honoring Pillay in 2022, and the event was canceled, according to The Times of Israel.

Bayefsky also recalled the 2009 U.N. anti-racism conference in Geneva, when Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad delivered an inflammatory speech attacking Israel. While Western diplomats walked out, Pillay remained seated.
However, Pillay subsequently condemned his address, saying she joined the secretary-general in "utterly deploring the speech," according to the U.N.'s official transcript.

"Her after-the-fact denunciation was utterly disingenuous." Bayefsky claimed, "Pillay had been given Ahmadinejad’s speech, questioning the veracity of the Holocaust and talking about the "ugly faces" of Zionists, in advance and yet still handed him the microphone as Conference Secretary-General."

The Nobel Committee, meanwhile, defended Pillay's legacy, crediting her with strengthening international law at a time when the institutions responsible for enforcing it face increasing political pressure.

Pillay's selection highlights the divide between supporters who celebrate her contributions to international justice and critics who contend that her record on Israel undermines the universal human rights principles she championed.

Navi Pillay, who won the Nobel Peace Prize Oct. 9, 2026, speaks during a briefing to U.N. member states about ongoing investigations of the Commission at the U.N. offices in Geneva April 16, 2024. (Fabrice Coffrini/AFP)
Fox News Digital reached out to Pillay for comment but didn’t receive one in time for publication.

title: Thousands flood Brussels streets as anti-austerity protests erupt into clashes with police
summary: Masked agitators clashed with riot police in Brussels as thousands of others marched against Belgium's austerity measures and cost of living crisis.
story: Belgian citizens against government budget cuts took to the streets on Friday in Brussels, clashing with police.

Thousands of demonstrators poured into the streets of Brussels on Friday, at times clashing with police officers, to protest the Belgian government's budget-tightening measures and the overall rise in the cost of living.

Dozens of protesters, most of them young and dressed in black with masks over their faces, were seen throwing rocks and firecrackers at police at the central Brussels railway station, The Associated Press reported.
They also set several fires, with photos showing a man lighting an electric scooter ablaze.

A man sets a shared electric scooter on fire during a national protest against the Belgian government's planned budget measures in Brussels, Belgium, on Oct. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Geert Vanden Wijngaert)
MAY DAY PROTESTS ACROSS EUROPE AND ASIA TURN INTO ANTI-AMERICAN, ANTI-ISRAEL POLITICAL BATTLEGROUNDS

Riot police responded by deploying tear gas canisters and shooting water cannons, tactics that dispersed the crowds. The chaos in the streets contributed to increased traffic across the Belgian capital.
Police said the unrest was caused by people unaffiliated with the anti-austerity demonstration, which drew an estimated 30,000 participants, the AP reported.

Two of Belgium’s largest labor unions organized Friday’s daylong national strike, with a separate public-sector walkout planned for Monday. Union leaders also distanced themselves from the unrest, saying those responsible were not affiliated with their movement.
Protesters clash with riot police during a national demonstration against government budget cuts and proposed reforms in Brussels, Belgium, on Oct. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Geert Vanden Wijngaert)

Union members and their supporters were dressed in red or green as they marched peacefully throughout the city.

title: Feds seized Rep. Ilhan Omar’s phone, subpoenaed family members in immigration status probe
summary: Federal agents seized Democratic Rep.
story: Federal agents seized Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s phone when they searched her Washington, D.C., home this week as part of a federal investigation into potential immigration-related crimes, and have sent roughly a dozen subpoenas out in the case, according to two people familiar with the investigation.
The possible charges cited by federal officials included conspiracy and making false statements in immigration paperwork, one of the people said.

The search came just three weeks before the midterms, within the window of time when the Justice Department has typically avoided overt actions in criminal cases that could impact an election. And the seizure of the phone of a sitting member of Congress would typically trigger a set of law enforcement protocols meant to ensure investigators aren’t infringing upon the “speech or debate” clause of the U.S. Constitution, which protects members of Congress from being questioned for their legislative acts.
On Friday, roughly a dozen subpoenas were sent out in the case, including to her family members, the second person familiar with the investigation told NBC News.

The congresswoman herself was not subpoenaed, the person said, adding that the orders seeking information are tied to a federal grand jury in Minnesota, Omar’s home state. Federal agents also want to talk to Omar’s sister but haven’t reached her yet, the person said.
The New York Times first reported on the subpoenas.
The investigation is being conducted by Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. attorney in Minneapolis and the Justice Department.
For Subscribers
A spokesperson for Omar didn’t respond to a request for comment. The Justice Department declined to comment.
Omar said in a statement posted online on Monday that she would not be silenced.

“Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement. For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation,” she wrote.

One of the people familiar with the investigation said it involved whistleblowers, documents and witness testimony. The probe is examining matters surrounding Omar’s immigration status, including — but not limited to — her birthdate. Omar, who was born in Somalia and moved to the United States with her family in the 1990s, was naturalized when she was 17 years old, meaning she was a juvenile and could be conferred citizenship through a parent.
For Subscribers

A criminal investigation could be complicated by the statute of limitations, which is typically five years, but investigators could look into Omar’s or her family members’ more recent actions that would fall within the statute of limitations.

Omar, who is part of a group of progressive women in Congress known as “the Squad,” has been a frequent target of Trump’s rhetoric against her and other members’ liberal positions, as well as Somali immigrants broadly.
Asked Monday if he had been aware of the search in advance, Trump said the federal government was looking at Omar “very carefully.” He also repeated his frequent attacks on her and Somalia.
“Then she comes over here and she complains about our Constitution,” Trump said. “I think she’s a terrible person, but that’s really up to the DOJ.”
That evening, Trump also attacked Omar in remarks at a rally he held for Republicans in Ohio.

“I don’t know what they’re doing with it, but I can tell you this: She’s a disaster,” Trump said. “She comes in from a country without laws, without police, without military, where all they do is shoot each other, and she comes into our country and she says, ‘I have a constitutional right.’”
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin appeared to tease federal action against Omar last month when he said “something’s going to happen” with her, but they were still investigating.

“If we actually move a case forward, it’s not a political case,” Mullin said. “It’s an actual case because they did things wrong. If you decided to break the law or lie [about] the information you gave the United States to be able to come into the United States through either asylum or because you were just wanting to seek a better life, but you didn’t tell us who you actually were, you lied about certain things about your application — those things, there’s no expiration to that.”

title: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of restricting Starlink, disrupting military amid Trump pressure
summary: Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of undermining its ability to defend itself by limiting Starlink internet services, as the country reeled from intense Russian ballistic missile attacks that it said came without the usual advance warning from allies.
story: Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of undermining its ability to defend itself by limiting Starlink internet services, as the country reeled from intense Russian ballistic missile attacks that it said came without the usual advance warning from allies.

Elon Musk put the responsibility for the restrictions on Trump’s shoulders in a social media post, saying the military version of Starlink, called Starshield, is owned and controlled by the U.S. government.
“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said.
A spokesperson for President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News that the limitations remained in place late Wednesday.

Facing pressure from President Donald Trump to halt strikes on Russia’s energy industry, Kyiv and its backers have worried Washington could cut off battlefield support to try and force it into concessions at the negotiating table.

Ukrainian officials and their European partners were already scrambling to understand the status of U.S. intelligence sharing after the lack of alert ahead of two Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv this week, two Ukrainian and two European officials told NBC News.

Trump insisted the U.S. was still sharing intel, but with relations spiraling Ukrainian officials and military units were on Wednesday accusing SpaceX of throttling a technology essential to their battlefield communications and drone operations.
It was not immediately clear what might be behind the Starlink interruptions, though some Ukrainian officials said the timing could not be a coincidence given that Musk is a close Trump ally.

title: Justice Department threatens legal action against California over alleged noncitizen voters
summary: The Justice Department is threatening legal action against California unless state and local officials review a list of potential noncitizens on their voter rolls.
story: WASHINGTON — The Justice Department is threatening legal action against California unless state and local officials review a list of potential noncitizens on their voter rolls.

Acting Deputy Attorney General R. Trent McCotter sent letters to California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan on Tuesday demanding that they review a list of possible noncitizens the federal government identified by noon on Thursday.

“Allowing noncitizens to vote cancels citizen votes,” McCotter wrote in letter, which was obtained by NBC News. “States are responsible for voter registration, and the Federal Government is responsible for maintaining immigration records to enable verification of citizenship. Working together, we can more effectively protect against voter dilution and promote election integrity.”

McCotter wrote that they provided a password-protected thumb drive with a list of individuals the federal government “believes are likely noncitizens who were sent a vote-by-mail ballot” for the 2026 election. He asked that election officials “segregate — not cancel — those individuals’ vote-by-mail ballots” until their citizenship status was determined.

“The Department of Justice sent letters to California election officials demanding immediate action to ensure that noncitizens who automatically received ballots per California law do not vote in the upcoming federal election,” a Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement. “This should not be controversial, as the criminal statute is clear: only American citizens may vote in federal elections. It is a federal crime for noncitizens to vote in U.S. elections, and the DOJ is asking California to ensure that is not occurring.”
Reuters first reported on the letters. Weber and Logan did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
All registered voters in California receive mail-in ballots, which started going out on Oct. 5.

The legal threats came amid a broader campaign by the Trump administration to zero in on what voting experts say is a relatively rare phenomenon of voting by noncitizens. Trump has long made unfounded claims that voting is marred by widespread fraud.
Election officials in a several states — including Georgia, Connecticut, Nevada, and Washington state — say they have received federal subpoenas in recent months for election records.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Some officials said they fear these actions were designed to set up possible legal challenges after the midterm elections.

“What we have seen is some groundwork laid out for post-election challenges,” said Stuart Holmes, the director of elections in Washington State. “Whether that’s the seizure of voting equipment, ballots themselves, tabulation equipment ...  we’re preparing for any and all eventualities in that case.”

Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, a Democrats said officials in his state are also preparing for potential challenges to this November’s results. He added that he viewed the administration’s moves as “an effort to dissuade people from participating in the elections.”

“You have a president who’s trying to choose the voter base rather than the voters choosing the elected, and that’s not how our democracy works,” he said in an interview. “It’s the people control our elections, and when you try to take that control out, you do it through intimidation, you do it through threats, and you do it by trying to dissuade people from participating.”

Since Trump took office, his administration has brought over 100 cases involving allegations of voting by non-citizens. More than 154 million people voted in the 2024 election, according to the U.S. Census Bureau.

During the second Trump administration, The Justice Department has sought voter registration data from every state in the country. It has filed lawsuits against 30 states and Washington, D.C., for refusing.

title: Social Security recipients will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living increase in 2027
summary: Individual retirement benefits will climb an average of about $75 per month, according to an advocacy group.
story: Social Security recipients will receive an annual cost-of-living adjustment next year of 3.6%, one of the largest increases this decade. But advocates say it’s still unlikely to go far enough for many struggling older adults.
It’s the largest adjustment since 2022 and will amount to an additional $75.15 per month on average, according to the Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group for older Americans.

Elevated inflation continues to bedevil the U.S. economy, with rising energy and gas prices sparked by the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars as the primary culprits. Yet even without the added cost of gas, so-called core inflation — which excludes volatile energy and food prices — has remained stuck at about 2.5%, well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target.

For older adults, who are the majority of Social Security retirement benefit recipients, next year’s increase will be welcome, but it will still come up short given rising costs, said Shannon Benton, the league’s executive director.
“Seniors have spent years watching their expenses outpacing their benefits,” Benton said. “This provides a little breathing room but won’t undo the damage of what we’ve seen this decade.”

The league found in a survey that 89% of older Americans thought the cost-of-living adjustment that kicked in this year, 2.8%, was inadequate given rising costs in the economy. About 44% of older adults draw all their income from Social Security, the survey found.
For Subscribers

The annual adjustment is typically calculated using inflation data from July, August and September. But it uses an obscure inflation index that advocates say doesn’t accurately reflect older adults’ spending priorities, which include more medical and prescription drug costs, as well as a greater likelihood that they will pay rent and generally higher home energy costs.
For Subscribers

Those categories have historically outpaced headline inflation, though the rate of medical-cost increases has slowed recently. One reform proposal would index the annual adjustment to more precisely reflect older adults’ needs — but Benton said it is unlikely to be adopted until all of Social Security is overhauled.
“They need Social Security benefits to cover the cost of living, and it’s just not happening,” she said.

title: Romance scammers are getting harder to catch. The consequences are costly.
summary: For people looking for love online, a match with a scammer could cost them their life savings.
story: For people looking for love online, a match with a scammer could cost them their life savings.

A congressional investigation, which began in September 2025 and lasted about a year, found that Tinder’s scam detection systems struggled for years to keep fraudulent accounts off the dating app. Parent company Match Group has since moved to address the shortcomings with new verification requirements and upgraded detection technology.
Romance scams have become a leading form of financial fraud in the U.S., costing Americans nearly $1.5 billion in reported losses last year, according to the Federal Trade Commission.

“There’s a lot of stigma to being a victim to scams,” Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., who launched the investigation alongside Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., said in an interview last week. “People should understand that really sophisticated people who are doing all the right things are still getting scammed because of the level of technology and resources that these criminal enterprises now do.”

Scammers today can realistically pose as representatives from familiar organizations like the local YMCA or a bank, and the accessibility of AI tools makes it easier than ever to research family members and mimic their voices. But romance scams, Hassan said, can be particularly emotionally devastating.

That was the case for Pennsylvania resident Sue Nuss, who told Congress’ Joint Economic Committee about her experience turning to Tinder in search of companionship after she lost her husband. There, she met a man who claimed to be from New Jersey.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
I fell prey because of my personality and because I was lonely. And I was very ashamed of what happened.
-Sue nuss, who spoke to Congress’ Joint Economic Committee about her experience turning to Tinder in search of companionship.
Nuss told NBC News that, over a month and a half, he won her trust with words that made her feel like he really “sees” and “understands” her.

The committee’s report, published Tuesday, stated that the man duped Nuss with a series of “fabricated” crises: job problems on an oil rig, an arrest in Mexico, his mom’s stroke and even her funeral — all excuses to ask Nuss, 77, for money. When the scammers behind the profile tried to trick her into believing the man she was dating had died, she said, she realized it was all a scam.

“I have always been a very giving person my entire life, and I’ve always been a caregiver,” Nuss told NBC News last week. “And I fell prey. I was very vulnerable. I fell prey because of my personality and because I was lonely. And I was very ashamed of what happened.”
Days after what she thought was a budding online relationship fell apart, Nuss’ scammer showed back up on Tinder with the same profile, she said in an interview.

Soon, another group approached her claiming they could recover what she had lost. Then, through an elaborate cryptocurrency scheme, that group managed to scam even more money from Nuss. She believes both scammer groups were connected, the report stated. It added that, in total, she lost more than $700,000.

“I struggle. Some days are really bad days and some days are good days. I do get therapy. I’m starting a very special therapy next week called EMDR because it’s a trauma,” Nuss said. “I don’t trust my decisions now.”

Congress last month passed the Romance Scam Prevention Act, which would require online dating service providers to notify and warn any users who get messaged by potential scammers. The bill awaits President Donald Trump’s signature.

This summer, Hassan also introduced legislation with Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., to create a central reporting portal for victims of scams, an initiative that she said could give the federal government the tools to detect patterns in scams to shut them down more effectively.
Scammers stole more than $1 trillion globally in one year, according to a 2024 report from the Global Anti-Scam Alliance.

“Enterprises that run scams are now costing the global economy more than the illicit drug trade does,” Hassan said. “This is really important for individuals. It’s really important for our economy. And so, the more people speak up about the need to change the way the federal government handles scams, the faster it’s going to happen.”

The Joint Economic Committee’s investigation sought to combat the prevalence of romance scams on platforms owned by Match Group, the biggest online dating company in the world, with a portfolio that includes Tinder, Hinge, Match and Plenty of Fish.

It found that during the first nine months of 2025, nearly 1.5 million scammers or other bad actors on Tinder and Hinge matched with someone. Nearly 500,000 of those accounts then exchanged contact information with other users.

Internal documents shared voluntarily with the committee noted that most of Tinder’s machine-learning detection scam models hadn’t been updated in years, and Match Group staff members found that scammers could quickly circumvent the company’s patchwork detection rules. Excessive false positives also overwhelmed the human moderators trying to detect dangerous accounts.
The committee wrote that it welcomes the changes Match Group has made to address those concerns.

Match Group deployed new detection models throughout the latter half of 2025 and the first half of 2026 to better catch bad actors, according to the committee’s report. This year, it introduced 169 automated rules and “improved” 108 others aimed at targeting and removing inauthentic actors.

One of its key rollouts is a mandatory biometric face check for all new users on Tinder and Hinge, meant to prevent users from making multiple accounts and ensure banned users can’t make new accounts.

Yoel Roth, Match Group’s senior vice president of trust and safety, told NBC News the company is “grateful the Committee recognized our significant advancements to protect our users against romance scams.”

“That said, the report mischaracterizes both the historical scale of our investment and the work already completed. Alongside our engagement with the Committee over the past year, we’ve made the largest safety advancements in Match Group’s history,” Roth wrote in a statement. “Trust and Safety is a foundational priority, and we intend to continue leading the industry in building tools that promote authentic, safe connections.”

Much of that safety work, including the face checks, was already underway before the committee’s investigation, according to Match Group. It reports having seen a roughly 60% reduction in exposure to bad actors in every market since the face checks began.
Hassan similarly said those measures have “already been successful in dramatically reducing the number of matches that their customers have with a scammer.”

“They need to do more, though, because there are still gaps in their systems,” she added. “And they are going to need to stay vigilant in new ways, because the criminals are always changing their technology and their tactics, too.”

title: It’s doll coming back to me now: Celine Dion gets her own Barbie
summary: Celine Dion is being made into a Barbie doll, one that will be sought by fans near, far, wherever they are.
story: Celine Dion is being made into a doll, one that will be sought by fans near, far, wherever they are.

The maker of Barbie announced it was releasing a special edition doll of Dion, 58, as part of its Mattel Creations line. The toy is modeled after the Canadian singer’s 1998 Oscars performance, where she sang “My Heart Will Go On” from James Cameron’s “Titanic” film.
Dion’s doll form has the same hair style, long-sleeved gown from her performance, as well as the Heart of the Ocean, the necklace that was famously featured in the movie.
The company announced the doll in an Instagram post and urged consumers not to wait. The caption noted that “she’s limited and she’s legendary.”

The doll is the latest celebration of the 58-year-old’s career after Dion revealed she’d been diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder. She announced in 2022 that she had stiff-person syndrome, telling fans in a video that the disease was causing painful spasms that it made it difficult for her to walk.

“Unfortunately, these spasms affect every aspect of my daily life, sometimes causing difficulties when I walk and not allowing me to use my vocal chords to sing the way I’m used to,” Dion said at the time.
But Dion refused to allow the disease to stop her from singing.

In 2024, she performed at the top of the Eiffel Tower in Paris for the Summer Olympics opening ceremony with her rendition of French singer Édith Piaf’s iconic “Hymne à l’amour.” Fans around the world were moved to see the singer triumph over her medical condition.
Singer Kelly Clarkson, who was serving as a co-host for NBC’s broadcast, struggled to find the words that could describe the emotion of the scene.

“If you know anything just about Celine right now ... this is her purpose. And if you know anything about what she’s going through right now and — I’m so sorry, I’m trying to hold it together — but that she got through that, that was incredible,” Clarkson said at the time, calling her a “gold winner for vocal athletes.”
Dion returned to the stage again last month in a series of comeback concerts. It was the first of a 26-show residency in Paris where Dion gave fans a taste of some of her greatest hits.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Among the songs chosen for the setlist was “All by Myself,” one of the most difficult vocal performances in Dion’s extensive catalogue of ballads. One American fan described the show to  NBC News as a “victory lap.”
“I think her belief is renewed, I think her spirit is renewed,” said Francesca Pezzulo.

title: Social media star Bryce Hall faces felony domestic violence charge in Las Vegas
summary: Social media star Bryce Hall faces a felony domestic violence charge following an incident in Nevada.
story: Social media star Bryce Hall faces a felony domestic violence charge following an incident in Nevada.
Hall, 26, is charged with domestic battery and coercion involving domestic violence with threat or use of physical force, Las Vegas court records show.
The alleged incident happened on July 27, but the case wasn’t filed until Aug. 28.
For Subscribers

“These allegations are false,” a representative for Hall told NBC News. “We look forward to the facts coming out in court. We’ll be taking legal action against those responsible for spreading false and defamatory claims.”
An arrest warrant was issued on Sept. 10, and Hall was ordered to have no contact with the victim, the court records show.
For Subscribers
Hall is known for making social media videos on YouTube and TikTok, where he has more than 22.8 million followers.

If you or someone you know is facing domestic violence, call the National Domestic Violence hotline for help at (800) 799-SAFE (7233), or go to www.thehotline.org for more. States often have domestic violence hotlines, as well.

title: Brooklyn store in Kelly Clarkson feud says Molly the mechanical bird is now on sale for $15 million
summary: A Brooklyn novelty shop made it clear Sunday that Molly, a singing and dancing mechanical bird that serves as its unofficial mascot, was not for sale after an incident with Kelly Clarkson.
story: A Brooklyn novelty shop made it clear Sunday that Molly, a singing and dancing mechanical bird that serves as its unofficial mascot, was not for sale after an incident with Kelly Clarkson.
But on Tuesday, the store changed its tune. Molly can now be purchased — for $15 million.
Adam Rubin, one of the shop’s co-owners, spoke with reporters Tuesday outside the Atlantic Avenue store and confirmed the hefty price tag.
Rubin declined to comment Wednesday. Clarkson did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

Molly, social media’s latest celebrity, entered the zeitgeist over the weekend after Clarkson shared what she described as a distasteful experience at the Brooklyn store on social media minutes after visiting.
In a lengthy post, she claimed she “drove all the way to Brooklyn” to check out Art of Play, only to be shooed away when she inquired about purchasing Molly, as if she couldn’t afford the bird.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman,” Clarkson said.
According to Art of Play, however, that’s not what happened.

In its own social media post Sunday, the store said Clarkson asked about buying Molly, but that wasn’t an option since the automaton bird is permanently affixed to a wall. The store said it told Clarkson that Molly wasn’t for sale.

“Sure, it wasn’t for sale. That’s the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with,” Clarkson shot back with another post Sunday. She said that she asked whether Molly was for sale while pointing to a nearby tag that appeared to list a price for the automaton. She said she was told Molly would cost $15,000 and that the store could find something comparable for her at a lower price point.
A photo of the purported price tag circulated online, and Clarkson included it in her second post.
Art of Play then released a second post Monday to “clarify some additional details about Kelly Clarkson’s visit.”

The shop said Clarkson was in the store for only five minutes, and that after she asked about Molly, an employee explained that while that bird was not for sale, “a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle.” Kolb has not responded to multiple requests for comment sent by NBC News.
“He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000,” the store employee continued. “We explained all of this to Kelly Clarkson.”
The shop said it also offered to show her a bird priced at $2,000 that she could take home the same day, but that she “did not stick around long enough to see it.”

Art of Play has since received a lot of attention. Journalist Pablo Torre obtained surveillance video of Clarkson in the store. Another creator who goes by Sober Facts accused the store of racial profiling.
All of this led Rubin, the shop owner, to gather reporters Tuesday morning to set the record straight.
‘Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger’

According to a condensed transcription of the impromptu news conference published by Curbed, Rubin called the incident “an insane misunderstanding” and “asymmetrical social warfare.” He also accused Clarkson of “scolding our shopkeeper on the way out.”
When asked whether the shopkeeper told Clarkson that Molly wasn’t for sale, Rubin punted twice.

“If this tweetstorm had not happened, we wouldn’t have realized there was a negative interaction in the shop; it was that undramatic,” he said, according to the transcript. “We treated her like a normal person, but apparently that didn’t live up to her expectations.”
Rubin explained that the artist, Kolb, takes years to create these one-of-a-kind birds, and it’s not easy to simply obtain one.
“This is not something that’s sitting in a warehouse. It’s like a piece of sculpture. It’s a fine-art piece,” he said.
But since Molly has gained so much attention, Rubin said, he’s willing to part with the bird for $15 million.

Despite Molly’s five minutes of fame, Art of Play said it has been dealing with “trolls.” The media has been camped outside, and friends and neighbors of the shop are being “attacked” and “doxed,” Rubin said.

“Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger,” Rubin said, adding that people are being “threatened on the street.” The store has turned off its phone due to the uptick in calls, but comments keep flooding its social media pages. True customers can’t get in touch.
“I want to be very clear about this,” Rubin said Tuesday. “Nobody who has ever visited this store in person is taking Kelly Clarkson’s side.”

Clarkson is a coach on NBC’s “The Voice” and the former host of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” which also aired on the network. NBC is a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of NBC News.

title: Woman stabbed young son and husband to death at Great Wolf Lodge, police say
summary: Metallica Rose Harrison killed her 3-year-old son and husband before failing to kill herself at  popular Pennsylvania water park Great Wolf Lodge, authorities said.
story: A woman killed her husband and 3-year-old son at a popular Pennsylvania water park before asking police for their help to die by suicide because she couldn’t “find the vein in her neck to stab,” authorities said Tuesday.

Officers rushed to the Great Wolf Lodge at 3:13 p.m. on Monday after a “distressed female” in Room 2030 “advised the dispatcher that she needed help committing suicide,” according to a Poconos Township Police Department statement.

That caller, 27-year-old Towanda resident Metallica Rose Harrison, told a dispatcher she wanted to die by suicide but needed help “to find the vein in her neck to stab,” according to a criminal complaint written by Detective Earl Ackerman.
Charles Harrison “suffered multiple stab wounds to the chest” while a 3-year-old child, identified only as “T.H.,” was found dead with a “single stab wound to the chest,” according to Ackerman.

She was taken to the hospital, accompanied by police, allegedly telling them in the ambulance that “everyday, I work so hard” to “be the best person, the best mother, the best wife,” the complaint said.
“‘It wasn’t supposed to end like this. I was supposed to have my happy family. That’s what I envisioned since I was a child, ’” according to Ackerman’s statement, quoting the suspect.
Harrison also asked how deep she needed to slice her wrist for the “next time,” the complaint said.
For Subscribers
Investigators found a “large butcher kitchen knife” in Room 2030’s bathroom floor and a “smaller knife” in the bathroom sink, the complaint said.
The family originally checked into Great Wolf on Sept. 21 and they were scheduled to leave on Tuesday.
The suspect allegedly told a dispatcher that police could find the bodies in their room with the complaint quoting her saying that “my husband and son are already gone in the bed in the living room.”
“They’re already gone, I’m sorry,” she said, according to the affidavit.
For Subscribers
Harrison was booked on suspicion of two counts of homicide.

“This case is an isolated domestic tragedy and there is no threat to the community,” according to the police statement. “Our thoughts and deepest condolences go out to the family and loved ones affected by this tragedy.”
The famed water park and child-friendly vacation destination is a little more than 100 miles north of central Philadelphia.
“We are deeply saddened and heartbroken by a tragic domestic incident that occurred yesterday in a guest room at our resort in the Pocono Mountains,” according to a Great Wold Lodge statement.
“It was an isolated family incident, and we’re cooperating fully with local law enforcement as they conduct their investigation. Our thoughts are with the family and loved ones of those affected.”
A judge ordered Harrison held without bail on Tuesday and it wasn’t immediately clear on Wednesday if she’d hired or been appointed an attorney to speak on her behalf.
Messages left at publicly listed phone numbers for the suspect and victim were not immediately returned on Wednesday.

If you or someone you know is in crisis, call 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.

title: Joni Mitchell becomes an American citizen after more than 60 years
summary: Joni Mitchell can see both sides of the U.S.-Canada border freely now.
story: Joni Mitchell can see both sides of the U.S.-Canada border freely now.

The famed Canadian singer-songwriter shared a major milestone with fans on Tuesday, posing with an American flag to reveal she is officially a U.S. citizen. She also shared a clip of her citizenship ceremony in the Instagram post.
“A journey that began 62 years ago,” Mitchell’s caption said.

Mitchell,  82, was born and raised in Canada before moving to the U.S. with her then-husband in the 1960s. She lived in Detroit and New York City before eventually settling in the Laurel Canyon area of Los Angeles.
Her fans might say that Mitchell is synonymous with California, considering her hit song named after the state on her beloved 1971 album “Blue.”
“Oh, California, I’m coming home,” Mitchell sang in the song. “Oh, make me feel good rock ‘n roll band. I’m your biggest fan. California, I’m coming home.”
And although Mitchell has not been a U.S. citizen until now, that hasn’t stopped her from speaking out about American politics.
She wrote “The Fiddle and the Drum” in 1969 in protest of the Vietnam war. Mitchell’s lyrics urged America to find peace as the world had “all come to fear the beating of your drum.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Mitchell also lashed out at tax exemptions for religious institutions in the 1980s in the song “Tax Free.” She called out the United States in the lyrics as well as religious leaders who call for large donations while “preaching love like hate.”

Most recently, Mitchell was on stage at the Hollywood Bowl in 2024 when she made her current political opinions clear. She was performing with singer Brandi Carlile, according to Billboard, when she told the crowd, “‘F--- Donald Trump.’ I love that song.”

title: Netflix to cut about 6% of worldwide staff
summary: Netflix is eliminating about 1,000 jobs in a round of layoffs, according to a source with knowledge of the matter.
story: Netflix is eliminating about 6% of its employee roster, or roughly 1,000 jobs, in a round of layoffs announced internally Wednesday, according to a source with knowledge of the matter and a company email seen by NBC News.

“Our mission — to entertain the world — is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” Netflix co-chief executives Greg Peters and Ted Sarandos said in the email to staff members Wednesday.
The news was first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The source with knowledge of the matter confirmed the newspaper’s reporting was accurate.

Netflix remains one of the titans of streaming, but it has struggled to boost user engagement on the platform. The service’s users watched more than 97 billion hours of content in the first half of 2026, an increase of 2% year over year, according to the company’s most recent quarterly earnings report.
“Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” Sarandos said at Bloomberg’s annual media conference late last month.
Netflix is expected to report its third-quarter financial results Tuesday.
The majority of the job cuts will be concentrated in Netflix’s product, technology, legal and human resources teams.
For Subscribers

Peters and Sarandos said the streaming firm will “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas” while also “making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees and investors.”
For Subscribers

In recent months, Netflix has looked for ways to boost subscriber engagement, including adding live sports programming and video podcasts licensed from third-party companies such as Bill Simmons’ The Ringer.
Netflix’s layoffs come as other major Hollywood studios look to reduce costs and streamline operations.

The Walt Disney Co. has cut hundreds of jobs this year under new CEO Josh D’Amaro, according to a source familiar with the matter. David Ellison’s Skydance is widely expected to shrink its workforce across Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.

title: Social Security recipients will receive a 3.6% cost-of-living increase in 2027
summary: Individual retirement benefits will climb an average of about $75 per month, according to an advocacy group.
story: Social Security recipients will receive an annual cost-of-living adjustment next year of 3.6%, one of the largest increases this decade. But advocates say it’s still unlikely to go far enough for many struggling older adults.
It’s the largest adjustment since 2022 and will amount to an additional $75.15 per month on average, according to the Senior Citizens League, an advocacy group for older Americans.

Elevated inflation continues to bedevil the U.S. economy, with rising energy and gas prices sparked by the Iran and Russia-Ukraine wars as the primary culprits. Yet even without the added cost of gas, so-called core inflation — which excludes volatile energy and food prices — has remained stuck at about 2.5%, well above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target.

For older adults, who are the majority of Social Security retirement benefit recipients, next year’s increase will be welcome, but it will still come up short given rising costs, said Shannon Benton, the league’s executive director.
“Seniors have spent years watching their expenses outpacing their benefits,” Benton said. “This provides a little breathing room but won’t undo the damage of what we’ve seen this decade.”

The league found in a survey that 89% of older Americans thought the cost-of-living adjustment that kicked in this year, 2.8%, was inadequate given rising costs in the economy. About 44% of older adults draw all their income from Social Security, the survey found.
For Subscribers

The annual adjustment is typically calculated using inflation data from July, August and September. But it uses an obscure inflation index that advocates say doesn’t accurately reflect older adults’ spending priorities, which include more medical and prescription drug costs, as well as a greater likelihood that they will pay rent and generally higher home energy costs.
For Subscribers

Those categories have historically outpaced headline inflation, though the rate of medical-cost increases has slowed recently. One reform proposal would index the annual adjustment to more precisely reflect older adults’ needs — but Benton said it is unlikely to be adopted until all of Social Security is overhauled.
“They need Social Security benefits to cover the cost of living, and it’s just not happening,” she said.

title: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of restricting Starlink, disrupting military amid Trump pressure
summary: Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of undermining its ability to defend itself by limiting Starlink internet services, as the country reeled from intense Russian ballistic missile attacks that it said came without the usual advance warning from allies.
story: Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of undermining its ability to defend itself by limiting Starlink internet services, as the country reeled from intense Russian ballistic missile attacks that it said came without the usual advance warning from allies.

Elon Musk put the responsibility for the restrictions on Trump’s shoulders in a social media post, saying the military version of Starlink, called Starshield, is owned and controlled by the U.S. government.
“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” Musk said.
A spokesperson for President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NBC News that the limitations remained in place late Wednesday.

Facing pressure from President Donald Trump to halt strikes on Russia’s energy industry, Kyiv and its backers have worried Washington could cut off battlefield support to try and force it into concessions at the negotiating table.

Ukrainian officials and their European partners were already scrambling to understand the status of U.S. intelligence sharing after the lack of alert ahead of two Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv this week, two Ukrainian and two European officials told NBC News.

Trump insisted the U.S. was still sharing intel, but with relations spiraling Ukrainian officials and military units were on Wednesday accusing SpaceX of throttling a technology essential to their battlefield communications and drone operations.
It was not immediately clear what might be behind the Starlink interruptions, though some Ukrainian officials said the timing could not be a coincidence given that Musk is a close Trump ally.

title: Do you actually need pet laundry detergent to clean your dog’s things?
summary: Pet laundry detergents are on the rise, but are they different from regular detergent? Veterinarians explain whether your dog or cat really needs it.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans.

Between muddy paws, drool, and the occasional accident, your dog’s bed, blankets, and toys can get dirty fast. And if you’ve shopped for laundry supplies lately, you may have noticed a growing number of detergents made specifically for pets, with promises to tackle odors and stains while being gentler on your dog’s skin.

But are they actually any different from the detergent you already use? Most of us aren’t looking to add another expense to our bills for household essentials. So I spoke to two veterinarians to find out what sets pet laundry detergents apart from regular ones, and which ones are the best if you find that you should be using one of these formulas to clean your furry friend’s things.
What is pet laundry detergent?

Pet laundry detergent is exactly what it sounds like: detergent sold with your pet’s things in mind. “Pet laundry detergents are products marketed specifically for washing things pets use, such as bedding, blankets, crate pads, washable toys, towels, and clothing,” says Dr. Jo Myers, a veterinarian at Vetster, a pet telehealth company.

That doesn’t mean your dog’s bed needs its own special soap, though. “Pet laundry detergent is more of a marketing term than a necessity, and most pets do not need a detergent specifically formulated for them,” says Dr. Liza Cahn, veterinarian at Embrace Pet Insurance. “If owners do choose a pet-specific product, one potential benefit is that it may contain enzymes or other ingredients designed to break down pet-related stains and odors, which can be especially useful for washing bedding, towels, and toys.”
The best laundry detergents for pets

If you decide a pet-specific formula is right for your household, there are plenty of options to choose from. To help narrow them down, I rounded up highly-rated pet laundry detergents. Each made-for-pets detergent in this list is designed to tackle the stains and odors that come with washing your dog’s (or cat’s) bedding, blankets, and toys. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans uses this detergent for her entire family, including her 3-year-old silky terrier Minni. “Thankfully she doesn’t shed, but she does start to smell like a corn chip factory between baths. Every time I bathe her, I wash her blankets, harnesses, bedding and favorite toys in this,” she says. “I’ve never had an issue getting odors out — though, she is only 7 pounds. I just love that she isn’t particularly sensitive, so I don’t need to invest in anything outside of what we already buy.”

I recently switched my entire family over to this laundry detergent — including my 7-year-old French bulldog, Myko. It’s gentle enough for my kids, as well as Myko’s sensitive skin. French bulldogs are notoriously prone to allergies and Myko frequently has little red patches of irritation. The last thing I want is lingering detergent on her favorite blanket or harness to further inflame her skin. This detergent is free of chemicals, but still manages to get out gross pet odors, stains and more.
What is the difference between pet detergent and regular laundry detergent?

Despite the special labels, pet laundry detergents may not be all that different from what’s already in your laundry room. “Veterinary hospitals have been washing enormous quantities of animal bedding for a very long time without requiring a special category of pet detergent,” says Myers. “Based on the evidence we currently have, I wouldn’t tell pet owners they need a special detergent simply because the laundry belongs to their pet.”

In fact, public health guidance points to the detergent you already own. “The CDC’s guidance on cleaning and disinfecting pet supplies specifically recommends ordinary laundry detergent for machine-washing soft pet items and says it’s okay to wash pet items with your clothes,” says Myers. “For pets described as having sensitive skin, the CDC says detergent without dyes or fragrance may be a good choice.” So if your dog’s skin is easily irritated, a free-and-clear formula, whether or not it’s labeled for pets, may be the better pick.
Frequently asked questions

Pet laundry detergent will work on most of the soft goods your dog uses every day. “Basically, you can use pet laundry detergent on anything belonging to your pet that the manufacturer says can go in the wash, including removable bed covers, blankets, crate pads, towels, washable fabric toys, and pet clothing,” says Myers.
Before you toss something in, check its care label for washing and drying instructions, since some items, like beds with foam inserts, may need to be washed in pieces or by hand.

“Some breeds are more likely to develop allergic and other skin diseases, but that’s not the same thing as certain breeds needing special laundry detergent,” says Myers. That said, Cahn does say that certain breeds have a  higher predisposition to atopic dermatitis and other skin problems, including bulldogs, Boston terriers, boxers, Chinese shar-peis, dalmatians, golden retrievers, labrador retrievers, Lhasa apsos, Scottish terriers, shih tzus, and West Highland white terriers.
“For a dog with diagnosed allergies or otherwise sensitive skin, it is reasonable to choose an unscented, dye-free detergent, and make sure that the laundry is thoroughly rinsed,” says Cahn.
